rows.en: We can read of things that happened 5,000 years ago in the Near East, where people first learned to write.
rows.zh: 我们能读到五千年前发生在近东的事情，人类最早就是在那里学会书写的。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: But there are some parts of the world where even now people cannot write.
rows.zh: 但世界上有些地方的人，直到今天仍不会书写。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The only way that they can preserve their history is to recount it as sagas—legends handed down from one generation of storytellers to another.
rows.zh: 他们保存自身历史的唯一办法，是把它讲成传说故事——由一代讲故事的人传给下一代的传奇。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: These legends are useful because they can tell us something about migrations of people who lived long ago, but none could write down what they did.
rows.zh: 这些传说很有用，因为它们能让我们了解一些远古人群迁徙的情况；当时那些人却没有一个能把自己的所作所为记下来。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Anthropologists wondered where the remote ancestors of the Polynesian peoples now living in the Pacific Islands came from.
rows.zh: 人类学家曾想知道，如今居住在太平洋群岛上的波利尼西亚各族的远祖究竟来自何处。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The sagas of these people explain that some of them came from Indonesia about 2,000 years ago.
rows.zh: 这些民族的传说讲述，其中一部分人大约在两千年前来自印度尼西亚。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: But the first people who were like ourselves lived so long ago that even their sagas, if they had any, are forgotten.
rows.zh: 然而，最早那些与我们相似的人生活的年代过于久远，就连他们的传说——假如他们有传说的话——也早已被遗忘了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: So archaeologists have neither history nor legends to help them to find out where the first ‘modern men’ came from.
rows.zh: 所以，考古学家既没有史料，也没有传说可借助，来查明最早的“现代人”来自哪里。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Fortunately, however, ancient men made tools of stone, especially flint, because this is easier to shape than other kinds.
rows.zh: 不过幸运的是，古人用石头制造工具，尤其常用燧石，因为它比其他石头容易加工成形。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: They may also have used wood and skins, but these have rotted away.
rows.zh: 他们也可能用过木材和兽皮，但这些东西都已腐烂。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Stone does not decay, and so the tools of long ago have remained when even the bones of the men who made them have disappeared without trace.
rows.zh: 石头不会腐朽，因此，哪怕制造工具的人的骨骼都已消失得无影无踪，那些远古的工具却仍保存了下来。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: read of 后接所读到的人或事情，侧重获知其存在或事迹。
usage.example: We can read of things that happened 5,000 years ago in the Near East, where people first learned to write.
usage.exampleZh: 我们能读到五千年前发生在近东的事情，人类最早就是在那里学会书写的。

usage.note: 常用被动形式；hand down from one generation to another 指代际传承。
usage.example: The only way that they can preserve their history is to recount it as sagas—legends handed down from one generation of storytellers to another.
usage.exampleZh: 他们保存自身历史的唯一办法，是把它讲成传说故事——由一代讲故事的人传给下一代的传奇。

usage.note: 指通过调查或探究获得答案，可接疑问词引导的从句。
usage.example: So archaeologists have neither history nor legends to help them to find out where the first ‘modern men’ came from.
usage.exampleZh: 所以，考古学家既没有史料，也没有传说可借助，来查明最早的“现代人”来自哪里。

usage.note: away 强调逐渐腐烂直至不复存在，适用于木材等有机物。
usage.example: They may also have used wood and skins, but these have rotted away.
usage.exampleZh: 他们也可能用过木材和兽皮，但这些东西都已腐烂。

usage.note: 通常用于消失等语境；也常说 without a trace。
usage.example: Stone does not decay, and so the tools of long ago have remained when even the bones of the men who made them have disappeared without trace.
usage.exampleZh: 石头不会腐朽，因此，哪怕制造工具的人的骨骼都已消失得无影无踪，那些远古的工具却仍保存了下来。

rows.en: Why, you may wonder, should spiders be our friends?
rows.zh: 你也许会纳闷，蜘蛛为什么应该算我们的朋友？
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Because they destroy so many insects, and insects include some of the greatest enemies of the human race.
rows.zh: 因为它们消灭的昆虫非常多，而昆虫中有些正是人类最大的敌人。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Insects would make it impossible for us to live in the world: they would devour all our crops and kill our flocks and herds, if it were not for the protection we get from insect-eating animals.
rows.zh: 要不是有食虫动物保护我们，昆虫会吞光我们的庄稼，杀死我们的牛羊牲畜，使我们根本无法在世上生存。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: We owe a lot to the birds and beasts who eat insects but all of them put together kill only a fraction of the number destroyed by spiders.
rows.zh: 我们很感激那些吃昆虫的鸟兽，但它们加在一起捕杀的昆虫，也仅是蜘蛛所消灭数量的一小部分。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Moreover, unlike some of the other insect eaters, spiders never do the least harm to us or our belongings.
rows.zh: 而且，与某些其他食虫动物不同，蜘蛛对我们和我们的财物丝毫无害。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Spiders are not insects, as many people think, nor even nearly related to them.
rows.zh: 蜘蛛并不像许多人以为的那样是昆虫，甚至与昆虫的亲缘关系也并不近。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: One can tell the difference almost at a glance, for a spider always has eight legs and an insect never more than six.
rows.zh: 人们几乎看一眼就能分清：蜘蛛总是有八条腿，而昆虫的腿从不超过六条。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: How many spiders are engaged in this work on our behalf?
rows.zh: 究竟有多少蜘蛛在替我们做这项工作呢？
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: One authority on spiders made a census of the spiders in a grass field in the south of England, and he estimated that there were more than 2,250,000 in one acre; that is something like 6,000,000 spiders of different kinds on a football pitch.
rows.zh: 一位蜘蛛研究权威曾清点英格兰南部一片草地里的蜘蛛，估算每英亩有二百二十五万只以上；也就是说，一块足球场大小的地方，大约有六百万只各种各样的蜘蛛。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Spiders are busy for at least half the year in killing insects.
rows.zh: 蜘蛛一年至少有半年都在忙着捕杀昆虫。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It is impossible to make more than the wildest guess at how many they kill, but they are hungry creatures, not content with only three meals a day.
rows.zh: 要说它们到底捕杀了多少昆虫，除了极不可靠的猜测，谁也无从估算；不过它们胃口很大，一天只吃三顿可满足不了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It has been estimated that the weight of all the insects destroyed by spiders in Britain in one year would be greater than the total weight of all the human beings in the country.
rows.zh: 据估计，英国蜘蛛一年消灭的全部昆虫，其重量会超过英国全体人口的体重总和。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: 用于与现在事实相反的假设，后接提供帮助或造成影响的人或事物。
usage.example: Insects would make it impossible for us to live in the world: they would devour all our crops and kill our flocks and herds, if it were not for the protection we get from insect-eating animals.
usage.exampleZh: 要不是有食虫动物保护我们，昆虫会吞光我们的庄稼，杀死我们的牛羊牲畜，使我们根本无法在世上生存。

usage.note: owe ... to ... 可表示把成就归功于某人，这里强调所受的恩惠。
usage.example: We owe a lot to the birds and beasts who eat insects but all of them put together kill only a fraction of the number destroyed by spiders.
usage.exampleZh: 我们很感激那些吃昆虫的鸟兽，但它们加在一起捕杀的昆虫，也仅是蜘蛛所消灭数量的一小部分。

usage.note: 作状语，表示不必仔细观察就能看出。
usage.example: One can tell the difference almost at a glance, for a spider always has eight legs and an insect never more than six.
usage.exampleZh: 人们几乎看一眼就能分清：蜘蛛总是有八条腿，而昆虫的腿从不超过六条。

usage.note: on someone’s behalf 也可表示替某人做事，此处是替人类消灭害虫。
usage.example: How many spiders are engaged in this work on our behalf?
usage.exampleZh: 究竟有多少蜘蛛在替我们做这项工作呢？

usage.note: with 后接名词或动名词；否定时表示不以现有数量或状况为满足。
usage.example: It is impossible to make more than the wildest guess at how many they kill, but they are hungry creatures, not content with only three meals a day.
usage.exampleZh: 要说它们到底捕杀了多少昆虫，除了极不可靠的猜测，谁也无从估算；不过它们胃口很大，一天只吃三顿可满足不了。

rows.en: Modern alpinists try to climb mountains by a route which will give them good sport, and the more difficult it is, the more highly it is regarded.
rows.zh: 现代登山者选择攀登路线时，追求的是攀登的乐趣与挑战；路线越难，评价就越高。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In the pioneering days, however, this was not the case at all.
rows.zh: 然而，在登山运动的开拓时期，情况完全不是这样。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The early climbers were looking for the easiest way to the top, because the summit was the prize they sought especially if it had never been attained before.
rows.zh: 早期登山者寻找的是最容易到达山顶的路，因为登顶才是他们追求的奖赏，尤其是此前从未有人登上过的山顶。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It is true that during their explorations they often faced difficulties and dangers of the most perilous nature, equipped in a manner which would make a modern climber shudder at the thought, but they did not go out of their way to court such excitement.
rows.zh: 诚然，他们探险时往往面临极其凶险的困难和危险，所携装备之简陋会让现代登山者想起来都打寒战；但他们并不会刻意去寻求这种刺激。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: They had a single aim, a solitary goal—the top!
rows.zh: 他们只有一个目的，一个唯一的目标——山顶！
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It is hard for us to realize nowadays how difficult it was for the pioneers.
rows.zh: 如今我们很难体会，那些先驱者当时有多么艰难。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Except for one or two places such as Zermatt and Chamonix, which had rapidly become popular, Alpine villages tended to be impoverished settlements cut off from civilization by the high mountains.
rows.zh: 除了采尔马特和夏蒙尼等一两个迅速兴盛起来的地方，阿尔卑斯山区的村庄大多是穷困的聚居地，被高山阻隔，与外界文明隔绝。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Such inns as there were were generally dirty and flea-ridden; the food simply local cheese accompanied by bread often twelve months old, all washed down with coarse wine.
rows.zh: 那寥寥几家客栈通常又脏又满是跳蚤；食物不过是当地的奶酪，配着往往已放了一年的面包，再用粗劣的葡萄酒把这些东西送下肚去。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Often a valley boasted no inn at all, and climbers found shelter wherever they could—sometimes with the local priest (who was usually as poor as his parishioners), sometimes with shepherds or cheese-makers.
rows.zh: 一个山谷常常连客栈都没有，登山者只能有什么地方就在哪里栖身——有时借住当地神父家中（神父通常和他的教民一样穷），有时住在牧羊人或奶酪制作人的家里。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Invariably the background was the same: dirt and poverty, and very uncomfortable.
rows.zh: 无论到哪里，周遭的情景总是一样：肮脏、贫穷，住着很不舒服。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: For men accustomed to eating seven-course dinners and sleeping between fine linen sheets at home, the change to the Alps must have been very hard indeed.
rows.zh: 这些人在家习惯吃有七道菜的正餐、睡铺着上等亚麻床单的床，来到阿尔卑斯山区后，生活上的改变必定让他们非常难受。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: the case 指前文所述的事实或情形；字典式用 not be the case，句中按时态变为 was not the case。
usage.example: In the pioneering days, however, this was not the case at all.
usage.exampleZh: 然而，在登山运动的开拓时期，情况完全不是这样。

usage.note: 后接 to do，表示超出正常需要去做某事。
usage.example: It is true that during their explorations they often faced difficulties and dangers of the most perilous nature, equipped in a manner which would make a modern climber shudder at the thought, but they did not go out of their way to court such excitement.
usage.exampleZh: 诚然，他们探险时往往面临极其凶险的困难和危险，所携装备之简陋会让现代登山者想起来都打寒战；但他们并不会刻意去寻求这种刺激。

usage.note: cut off 常用被动形式，from 引出无法联系或到达的外界。
usage.example: Except for one or two places such as Zermatt and Chamonix, which had rapidly become popular, Alpine villages tended to be impoverished settlements cut off from civilization by the high mountains.
usage.exampleZh: 除了采尔马特和夏蒙尼等一两个迅速兴盛起来的地方，阿尔卑斯山区的村庄大多是穷困的聚居地，被高山阻隔，与外界文明隔绝。

usage.note: wash food down with a drink 是饮食搭配，不是洗涤食物。
usage.example: Such inns as there were were generally dirty and flea-ridden; the food simply local cheese accompanied by bread often twelve months old, all washed down with coarse wine.
usage.exampleZh: 那寥寥几家客栈通常又脏又满是跳蚤；食物不过是当地的奶酪，配着往往已放了一年的面包，再用粗劣的葡萄酒把这些东西送下肚去。

usage.note: to 是介词，后接名词或动名词，如这里的 eating 和 sleeping。
usage.example: For men accustomed to eating seven-course dinners and sleeping between fine linen sheets at home, the change to the Alps must have been very hard indeed.
usage.exampleZh: 这些人在家习惯吃有七道菜的正餐、睡铺着上等亚麻床单的床，来到阿尔卑斯山区后，生活上的改变必定让他们非常难受。

rows.en: Several cases have been reported in Russia recently of people who can read and detect colours with their fingers, and even see through solid doors and walls.
rows.zh: 俄罗斯最近报道了几起事例：有人能用手指读字、辨认颜色，甚至能透过不透明的门和墙看见东西。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: One case concerns an eleven-year-old schoolgirl, Vera Petrova, who has normal vision but who can also perceive things with different parts of her skin, and through solid walls.
rows.zh: 其中一例涉及一名十一岁的女学生维拉·彼得罗娃；她视力正常，却还能用皮肤的不同部位感知事物，也能隔着实心墙感知东西。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: This ability was first noticed by her father.
rows.zh: 最先注意到这种能力的是她的父亲。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: One day she came into his office and happened to put her hands on the door of a locked safe.
rows.zh: 有一天，她走进父亲的办公室，碰巧把双手放在一只锁着的保险柜门上。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Suddenly she asked her father why he kept so many old newspapers locked away there, and even described the way they were done up in bundles.
rows.zh: 她突然问父亲为什么把那么多旧报纸锁在那里，甚至描述出了报纸捆扎成束的样子。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Vera's curious talent was brought to the notice of a scientific research institute in the town of Ulyanovsk, near where she lives, and in April she was given a series of tests by a special commission of the Ministry of Health of the Russian Federal Republic.
rows.zh: 维拉这种奇特的天赋引起了离她住处不远的乌里扬诺夫斯克市一家科研机构的注意；四月，俄罗斯联邦共和国卫生部的一个专门委员会对她进行了一系列测试。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: During these tests she was able to read a newspaper through an opaque screen and, stranger still, by moving her elbow over a child's game of Lotto she was able to describe the figures and colours printed on it; and, in another instance, wearing stockings and slippers, to make out with her foot the outlines and colours of a picture hidden under a carpet.
rows.zh: 测试中，她能隔着不透明的屏障读报；更奇怪的是，她把肘部从一种名叫乐透的儿童游戏上方移过，就能说出上面印的数字和颜色；另一次，她穿着袜子和拖鞋，还能用脚辨出藏在地毯下面的一幅画的轮廓和颜色。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Other experiments showed that her knees and shoulders had a similar sensitivity.
rows.zh: 其他实验表明，她的膝部和肩部也具有类似的感知能力。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: During all these tests Vera was blindfold; and, indeed, except when blindfold she lacked the ability to perceive things with her skin.
rows.zh: 这些测试进行时，维拉始终蒙着眼；事实上，只有蒙上眼时，她才具有用皮肤感知事物的能力。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It was also found that although she could perceive things with her fingers this ability ceased the moment her hands were wet.
rows.zh: 研究者还发现，虽然她能用手指感知东西，但只要双手一湿，这种能力就会消失。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: 后接动词原形，说明事件偶然发生，并非有意安排。
usage.example: One day she came into his office and happened to put her hands on the door of a locked safe.
usage.exampleZh: 有一天，她走进父亲的办公室，碰巧把双手放在一只锁着的保险柜门上。

usage.note: away 强调收起保管，常与柜子、贵重物品或文件相关。
usage.example: Suddenly she asked her father why he kept so many old newspapers locked away there, and even described the way they were done up in bundles.
usage.exampleZh: 她突然问父亲为什么把那么多旧报纸锁在那里，甚至描述出了报纸捆扎成束的样子。

usage.note: 常用被动形式，表示某情况被提交给机构或个人关注。
usage.example: Vera's curious talent was brought to the notice of a scientific research institute in the town of Ulyanovsk, near where she lives, and in April she was given a series of tests by a special commission of the Ministry of Health of the Russian Federal Republic.
usage.exampleZh: 维拉这种奇特的天赋引起了离她住处不远的乌里扬诺夫斯克市一家科研机构的注意；四月，俄罗斯联邦共和国卫生部的一个专门委员会对她进行了一系列测试。

usage.note: 此处是辨别模糊或被遮蔽的视觉信息，并非编造或填写。
usage.example: During these tests she was able to read a newspaper through an opaque screen and, stranger still, by moving her elbow over a child's game of Lotto she was able to describe the figures and colours printed on it; and, in another instance, wearing stockings and slippers, to make out with her foot the outlines and colours of a picture hidden under a carpet.
usage.exampleZh: 测试中，她能隔着不透明的屏障读报；更奇怪的是，她把肘部从一种名叫乐透的儿童游戏上方移过，就能说出上面印的数字和颜色；另一次，她穿着袜子和拖鞋，还能用脚辨出藏在地毯下面的一幅画的轮廓和颜色。

usage.note: 作时间连词使用，可直接连接从句，不必另加 when。
usage.example: It was also found that although she could perceive things with her fingers this ability ceased the moment her hands were wet.
usage.exampleZh: 研究者还发现，虽然她能用手指感知东西，但只要双手一湿，这种能力就会消失。

rows.en: People are always talking about ‘the problem of youth’.
rows.zh: 人们总在谈论“青年问题”。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: If there is one—which I take leave to doubt—then it is older people who create it, not the young themselves.
rows.zh: 假如确实有这个问题——对此我恕难苟同——制造问题的也是年长者，而不是青年自己。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Let us get down to fundamentals and agree that the young are after all human beings—people just like their elders.
rows.zh: 让我们从根本说起，承认青年归根到底也是人，是和长辈一样的人。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: There is only one difference between an old man and a young one: the young man has a glorious future before him and the old one has a splendid future behind him: and maybe that is where the rub is.
rows.zh: 老人和青年只有一点不同：青年面前有灿烂的未来，老人身后有过往那曾经辉煌的“未来”；也许症结就在这里。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: When I was a teenager, I felt that I was just young and uncertain—that I was a new boy in a huge school, and I would have been very pleased to be regarded as something so interesting as a problem.
rows.zh: 我十几岁时，只觉得自己年少而惶惑，像是刚进一所大学校的新生；倘若有人把我看作像“问题”那么引人关注的事物，我倒会非常高兴。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: For one thing, being a problem gives you a certain identity, and that is one of the things the young are busily engaged in seeking.
rows.zh: 首先，被当作一个问题能赋予你某种身份，而寻找自己的身份恰恰是青年正忙着做的事之一。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: I find young people exciting.
rows.zh: 我觉得青年令人振奋。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: They have an air of freedom, and they have not a dreary commitment to mean ambitions or love of comfort.
rows.zh: 他们身上有一股自由的气息，不会令人厌倦地执着于卑微的野心或贪图安逸。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: They are not anxious social climbers, and they have no devotion to material things.
rows.zh: 他们不是急于攀附上流社会的人，也不痴迷于物质。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: All this seems to me to link them with life, and the origins of things.
rows.zh: 在我看来，这一切使他们与生命、与万物的本源相联。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It’s as if they were, in some sense, cosmic beings in violent and lovely contrast with us suburban creatures.
rows.zh: 仿佛从某种意义上说，他们是宇宙中的生灵，与我们这些蜗居市郊的凡俗之辈形成强烈而可爱的对照。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: All that is in my mind when I meet a young person.
rows.zh: 每当我遇见一个青年，心中想到的就是这些。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He may be conceited, ill-mannered, presumptuous or fatuous, but I do not turn for protection to dreary clichés about respect for elders—as if mere age were a reason for respect.
rows.zh: 他可能自负、无礼、冒失或愚蠢，但我不会躲到那些乏味的“尊重长辈”之类的套话后面寻求庇护，仿佛年纪大本身就值得尊敬似的。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: I accept that we are equals, and I will argue with him, as an equal, if I think he is wrong.
rows.zh: 我承认我们是平等的；如果我认为他错了，就会以平等的身份和他辩论。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: 礼貌而带有反驳意味的表达，后接动词原形，此处表示不同意这种说法。
usage.example: If there is one—which I take leave to doubt—then it is older people who create it, not the young themselves.
usage.exampleZh: 假如确实有这个问题——对此我恕难苟同——制造问题的也是年长者，而不是青年自己。

usage.note: to 是介词，后接名词或动名词；此处指回到基本事实。
usage.example: Let us get down to fundamentals and agree that the young are after all human beings—people just like their elders.
usage.exampleZh: 让我们从根本说起，承认青年归根到底也是人，是和长辈一样的人。

usage.note: rub 在这个固定说法里表示困难或障碍，并非摩擦动作。
usage.example: There is only one difference between an old man and a young one: the young man has a glorious future before him and the old one has a splendid future behind him: and maybe that is where the rub is.
usage.exampleZh: 老人和青年只有一点不同：青年面前有灿烂的未来，老人身后有过往那曾经辉煌的“未来”；也许症结就在这里。

usage.note: 用于列举理由，不一定必须接 for another thing。
usage.example: For one thing, being a problem gives you a certain identity, and that is one of the things the young are busily engaged in seeking.
usage.exampleZh: 首先，被当作一个问题能赋予你某种身份，而寻找自己的身份恰恰是青年正忙着做的事之一。

usage.note: turn to someone/something for ... 中 for 短语可提前插入，此处有讽刺意味。
usage.example: He may be conceited, ill-mannered, presumptuous or fatuous, but I do not turn for protection to dreary clichés about respect for elders—as if mere age were a reason for respect.
usage.exampleZh: 他可能自负、无礼、冒失或愚蠢，但我不会躲到那些乏味的“尊重长辈”之类的套话后面寻求庇护，仿佛年纪大本身就值得尊敬似的。

rows.en: I am always amazed when I hear people saying that sport creates goodwill between the nations, and that if only the common peoples of the world could meet one another at football or cricket, they would have no inclination to meet on the battlefield.
rows.zh: 每当听到有人说体育能增进各国之间的友好，说只要世界各国的普通百姓能在足球场或板球场上相遇，就不会想在战场上相遇，我总是十分惊讶。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Even if one didn’t know from concrete examples (the 1936 Olympic Games, for instance) that international sporting contests lead to orgies of hatred, one could deduce it from general principles.
rows.zh: 即使我们不知道那些证明国际体育竞赛会引发仇恨狂潮的具体事例——例如一九三六年奥运会——也能从一般原理推导出这一点。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Nearly all the sports practised nowadays are competitive.
rows.zh: 如今开展的体育运动几乎全都有竞争性。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: You play to win, and the game has little meaning unless you do your utmost to win.
rows.zh: 参加比赛就是为了赢；若不竭尽全力争取获胜，比赛便没有多大意义。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: On the village green, where you pick up sides and no feeling of local patriotism is involved, it is possible to play simply for the fun and exercise: but as soon as the question of prestige arises, as soon as you feel that you and some larger unit will be disgraced if you lose, the most savage combative instincts are aroused.
rows.zh: 在村中的公共草地上，大家临时分队，也不牵涉地方荣誉感，完全可以只为娱乐和锻炼而玩；可是一旦关系到声望，一旦你觉得输了会让自己以及某个更大的集体蒙羞，最凶猛好斗的本能就会被激发出来。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Anyone who has played even in a school football match knows this.
rows.zh: 哪怕只参加过学校足球赛的人，也知道这一点。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: At the international level, sport is frankly mimic warfare.
rows.zh: 坦率地说，国际层面的体育就是模拟战争。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: But the significant thing is not the behaviour of the players but the attitude of the spectators: and, behind the spectators, of the nations who work themselves into furies over these absurd contests, and seriously believe—at any rate for short periods—that running, jumping and kicking a ball are tests of national virtue.
rows.zh: 但关键在于观众的态度，而不在于运动员的表现；观众背后还有各个国家，它们会为这些荒唐的比赛怒不可遏，并且认真地相信——至少在短时间内如此——跑步、跳跃和踢球能检验一个民族的优劣。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: 常表示愿望；此处转述一种带理想色彩的条件设想。
usage.example: I am always amazed when I hear people saying that sport creates goodwill between the nations, and that if only the common peoples of the world could meet one another at football or cricket, they would have no inclination to meet on the battlefield.
usage.exampleZh: 每当听到有人说体育能增进各国之间的友好，说只要世界各国的普通百姓能在足球场或板球场上相遇，就不会想在战场上相遇，我总是十分惊讶。

usage.note: deduce something from evidence/principles 表示依据证据或原则作推论。
usage.example: Even if one didn’t know from concrete examples (the 1936 Olympic Games, for instance) that international sporting contests lead to orgies of hatred, one could deduce it from general principles.
usage.exampleZh: 即使我们不知道那些证明国际体育竞赛会引发仇恨狂潮的具体事例——例如一九三六年奥运会——也能从一般原理推导出这一点。

usage.note: 后常接 to do，utmost 在此是名词，表示最大努力。
usage.example: You play to win, and the game has little meaning unless you do your utmost to win.
usage.exampleZh: 参加比赛就是为了赢；若不竭尽全力争取获胜，比赛便没有多大意义。

usage.note: mimic 在这里作形容词，表示模拟的；作者用这一搭配强调国际体育的对抗性质。
usage.example: At the international level, sport is frankly mimic warfare.
usage.exampleZh: 坦率地说，国际层面的体育就是模拟战争。

usage.note: 此处缩小断言范围，表示至少在短时间内确实如此。
usage.example: But the significant thing is not the behaviour of the players but the attitude of the spectators: and, behind the spectators, of the nations who work themselves into furies over these absurd contests, and seriously believe—at any rate for short periods—that running, jumping and kicking a ball are tests of national virtue.
usage.exampleZh: 但关键在于观众的态度，而不在于运动员的表现；观众背后还有各个国家，它们会为这些荒唐的比赛怒不可遏，并且认真地相信——至少在短时间内如此——跑步、跳跃和踢球能检验一个民族的优劣。

rows.en: Not all sounds made by animals serve as language, and we have only to turn to that extraordinary discovery of echo-location in bats to see a case in which the voice plays a strictly utilitarian role.
rows.zh: 动物发出的声音并非全都起语言的作用；只要看看蝙蝠回声定位这一非凡的发现，我们就能找到声音完全用于实际功用的一个例子。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: To get a full appreciation of what this means we must turn first to some recent human inventions.
rows.zh: 要充分理解这意味着什么，我们必须先看看人类近来的一些发明。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Everyone knows that if he shouts in the vicinity of a wall or a mountainside, an echo will come back.
rows.zh: 人人都知道，如果在墙壁或山坡附近喊一声，就会传回回声。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The further off this solid obstruction, the longer time will elapse for the return of the echo.
rows.zh: 这个坚实的障碍物离得越远，回声传回所需的时间就越长。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: A sound made by tapping on the hull of a ship will be reflected from the sea bottom, and by measuring the time interval between the taps and the receipt of the echoes, the depth of the sea at that point can be calculated.
rows.zh: 敲击船体产生的声音会从海底反射回来；测量敲击与接收到回声之间的时间间隔，就能算出该处海水的深度。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: So was born the echo-sounding apparatus, now in general use in ships.
rows.zh: 回声测深仪就是这样诞生的，如今它已在船上普遍使用。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Every solid object will reflect a sound, varying according to the size and nature of the object.
rows.zh: 任何固体都会反射声音，反射的声音随物体的大小和性质而异。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: A shoal of fish will do this.
rows.zh: 鱼群也会反射声音。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: So it is a comparatively simple step from locating the sea bottom to locating a shoal of fish.
rows.zh: 因此，从探测海底到探测鱼群，是比较容易跨出的一步。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: With experience, and with improved apparatus, it is now possible not only to locate a shoal but to tell if it is herring, cod, or other well-known fish, by the pattern of its echo.
rows.zh: 有了经验和改进后的仪器，如今人们不但能探测到鱼群，还能根据回声的特征判断它是鲱鱼、鳕鱼，还是其他常见鱼类。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It has been found that certain bats emit squeaks and by receiving the echoes, they can locate and steer clear of obstacles—or locate flying insects on which they feed.
rows.zh: 人们发现，某些蝙蝠会发出尖叫声，并通过接收回声确定障碍物的位置、避开障碍物，或找到它们赖以为食的飞虫。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: This echo-location in bats is often compared with radar, the principle of which is similar.
rows.zh: 蝙蝠的这种回声定位常被拿来与雷达相比，两者原理相似。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: as 后接名词，说明事物所起的作用或用途。
usage.example: Not all sounds made by animals serve as language, and we have only to turn to that extraordinary discovery of echo-location in bats to see a case in which the voice plays a strictly utilitarian role.
usage.exampleZh: 动物发出的声音并非全都起语言的作用；只要看看蝙蝠回声定位这一非凡的发现，我们就能找到声音完全用于实际功用的一个例子。

usage.note: 较正式的地点表达，vicinity 表示周围一带。
usage.example: Everyone knows that if he shouts in the vicinity of a wall or a mountainside, an echo will come back.
usage.exampleZh: 人人都知道，如果在墙壁或山坡附近喊一声，就会传回回声。

usage.note: in use 表示正在使用，general 进一步说明普及程度。
usage.example: So was born the echo-sounding apparatus, now in general use in ships.
usage.exampleZh: 回声测深仪就是这样诞生的，如今它已在船上普遍使用。

usage.note: 原指操纵方向以避障，也可比喻避开麻烦或某个话题。
usage.example: It has been found that certain bats emit squeaks and by receiving the echoes, they can locate and steer clear of obstacles—or locate flying insects on which they feed.
usage.exampleZh: 人们发现，某些蝙蝠会发出尖叫声，并通过接收回声确定障碍物的位置、避开障碍物，或找到它们赖以为食的飞虫。

usage.note: 原句将 on 提到关系代词 which 前面；常用结构是 animals feed on insects。
usage.example: It has been found that certain bats emit squeaks and by receiving the echoes, they can locate and steer clear of obstacles—or locate flying insects on which they feed.
usage.exampleZh: 人们发现，某些蝙蝠会发出尖叫声，并通过接收回声确定障碍物的位置、避开障碍物，或找到它们赖以为食的飞虫。

rows.en: Chickens slaughtered in the United States, claim officials in Brussels, are not fit to grace European tables.
rows.zh: 布鲁塞尔的官员声称，在美国宰杀的鸡不配登上欧洲人的餐桌。
rows.speaker: 布鲁塞尔官员

rows.en: No, say the Americans: our fowl are fine, we simply clean them in a different way.
rows.zh: 美国人却说：不，我们的禽肉很好，我们只是采用了不同的清洗方式。
rows.speaker: 美国方面

rows.en: These days, it is differences in national regulations, far more than tariffs, that put sand in the wheels of trade between rich countries.
rows.zh: 如今，阻碍富裕国家之间贸易的，与其说是关税，不如说更多是各国法规的差异。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It is not just farmers who are complaining.
rows.zh: 抱怨的并不只是农民。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: An electric razor that meets the European Union's safety standards must be approved by American testers before it can be sold in the United States, and an American-made dialysis machine needs the EU’s okay before it hits the market in Europe.
rows.zh: 一把达到欧盟安全标准的电动剃须刀，要先得到美国检测人员的认可才能在美国销售；而一台美国制造的透析机，也须经过欧盟批准才能进入欧洲市场。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: As it happens, a razor that is safe in Europe is unlikely to electrocute Americans.
rows.zh: 事实上，在欧洲使用安全的剃须刀，大概也不至于把美国人电死。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: So, ask businesses on both sides of the Atlantic, why have two lots of tests where one would do?
rows.zh: 所以，大西洋两岸的企业都问：一次检测既然就够了，何必检测两次？
rows.speaker: 美欧企业

rows.en: Politicians agree, in principle, so America and the EU have been trying to reach a deal which would eliminate the need to double-test many products.
rows.zh: 政界人士原则上表示赞同，因此美国和欧盟一直试图达成协议，让许多产品不再需要重复检测。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: They hope to finish in time for a trade summit between America and the EU on May 28th.
rows.zh: 他们希望及时完成谈判，赶上五月二十八日的美欧贸易峰会。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Although negotiators are optimistic, the details are complex enough that they may be hard-pressed to get a deal at all.
rows.zh: 谈判代表虽然乐观，但细节如此复杂，他们最终能否达成任何协议都大有困难。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Why?
rows.zh: 为什么呢？
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: One difficulty is to construct the agreements.
rows.zh: 其中一个难题是如何构建这些协议。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The Americans would happily reach one accord on standards for medical devices and then hammer out different pacts covering, say, electronic goods and drug manufacturing.
rows.zh: 美国人很乐意先就医疗器械标准达成一项协议，再艰苦协商出其他分别涵盖电子产品、药品制造等领域的协定。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The EU—following fine continental traditions—wants agreement on general principles, which could be applied to many types of products and perhaps extended to other countries.
rows.zh: 欧盟则遵循欧洲大陆一贯讲究原则的好传统，希望先就总原则达成一致，使之适用于多种产品，也许还能推广到其他国家。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: fit to do 表示适合做某事；此处与 grace 搭配，带有挑剔和讽刺色彩。
usage.example: Chickens slaughtered in the United States, claim officials in Brussels, are not fit to grace European tables.
usage.exampleZh: 布鲁塞尔的官员声称，在美国宰杀的鸡不配登上欧洲人的餐桌。

usage.note: hit 在此表示到达或出现，不是打击市场。
usage.example: An electric razor that meets the European Union's safety standards must be approved by American testers before it can be sold in the United States, and an American-made dialysis machine needs the EU’s okay before it hits the market in Europe.
usage.exampleZh: 一把达到欧盟安全标准的电动剃须刀，要先得到美国检测人员的认可才能在美国销售；而一台美国制造的透析机，也须经过欧盟批准才能进入欧洲市场。

usage.note: 用于引入恰好与讨论有关的事实，有时带反讽意味。
usage.example: As it happens, a razor that is safe in Europe is unlikely to electrocute Americans.
usage.exampleZh: 事实上，在欧洲使用安全的剃须刀，大概也不至于把美国人电死。

usage.note: 表示同意总体想法，未必已对具体执行细节取得一致。
usage.example: Politicians agree, in principle, so America and the EU have been trying to reach a deal which would eliminate the need to double-test many products.
usage.exampleZh: 政界人士原则上表示赞同，因此美国和欧盟一直试图达成协议，让许多产品不再需要重复检测。

usage.note: 常接 agreement、deal 等，强调协商过程费力。
usage.example: The Americans would happily reach one accord on standards for medical devices and then hammer out different pacts covering, say, electronic goods and drug manufacturing.
usage.exampleZh: 美国人很乐意先就医疗器械标准达成一项协议，再艰苦协商出其他分别涵盖电子产品、药品制造等领域的协定。

rows.en: Alfred the Great acted as his own spy, visiting Danish camps disguised as a minstrel.
rows.zh: 阿尔弗雷德大帝亲自充当间谍，乔装成吟游诗人，探访丹麦人的营地。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In those days wandering minstrels were welcome everywhere.
rows.zh: 那时候，四处游历的吟游诗人到哪里都受欢迎。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: They were not fighting men, and their harp was their passport.
rows.zh: 他们不是战士，手中的竖琴就是通行证。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Alfred had learned many of their ballads in his youth, and could vary his programme with acrobatic tricks and simple conjuring.
rows.zh: 阿尔弗雷德年轻时学会了他们的许多歌谣，还能穿插表演杂技和简单的魔术，使节目更加丰富。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: While Alfred’s little army slowly began to gather at Athelney, the king himself set out to penetrate the camp of Guthrum, the commander of the Danish invaders.
rows.zh: 阿尔弗雷德的小股部队在阿瑟尔尼慢慢集结时，国王本人动身潜入丹麦侵略军统帅古斯鲁姆的营地。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: These had settled down for the winter at Chippenham: thither Alfred went.
rows.zh: 丹麦军队已在奇彭纳姆安顿下来过冬，阿尔弗雷德便前往那里。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He noticed at once that discipline was slack: the Danes had the self-confidence of conquerors, and their security precautions were casual.
rows.zh: 他立刻发现营中纪律松弛：丹麦人有征服者的自信，安全戒备十分随便。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: They lived well, on the proceeds of raids on neighbouring regions.
rows.zh: 他们靠抢掠邻近地区所得的东西过着优裕生活。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: There they collected women as well as food and drink, and a life of ease had made them soft.
rows.zh: 他们在那里不仅掳来食物和酒，还掳来女人；安逸的生活已使他们变得软弱。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Alfred stayed in the camp a week before he returned to Athelney.
rows.zh: 阿尔弗雷德在敌营待了一周才返回阿瑟尔尼。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The force there assembled was trivial compared with the Danish horde.
rows.zh: 那里集结的兵力与丹麦大军相比，实在微不足道。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: But Alfred had deduced that the Danes were no longer fit for prolonged battle: and that their commissariat had no organization, but depended on irregular raids.
rows.zh: 但阿尔弗雷德已经推断出，丹麦人再也经不起持久作战；而且他们的军需补给毫无组织，只靠不定时的抢掠。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: So, faced with the Danish advance, Alfred did not risk open battle but harried the enemy.
rows.zh: 所以，面对丹麦军队的进逼，阿尔弗雷德没有冒险进行正面交战，而是不断袭扰敌人。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He was constantly on the move, drawing the Danes after him.
rows.zh: 他不停转移，引着丹麦人追赶。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: His patrols halted the raiding parties: hunger assailed the Danish army.
rows.zh: 他的巡逻队拦截了出来抢掠的队伍，饥饿开始侵袭丹麦军队。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Now Alfred began a long series of skirmishes—and within a month the Danes had surrendered.
rows.zh: 这时，阿尔弗雷德展开了一连串的小规模战斗；不到一个月，丹麦人便投降了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The episode could reasonably serve as a unique epic of royal espionage!
rows.zh: 这一段经历，完全可以称得上王者亲自从事谍报活动的一部独特史诗！
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: 常用 be disguised as，as 后接伪装的身份。
usage.example: Alfred the Great acted as his own spy, visiting Danish camps disguised as a minstrel.
usage.exampleZh: 阿尔弗雷德大帝亲自充当间谍，乔装成吟游诗人，探访丹麦人的营地。

usage.note: set out to do 可表示开始有目的的行动，此处兼有启程之意。
usage.example: While Alfred’s little army slowly began to gather at Athelney, the king himself set out to penetrate the camp of Guthrum, the commander of the Danish invaders.
usage.exampleZh: 阿尔弗雷德的小股部队在阿瑟尔尼慢慢集结时，国王本人动身潜入丹麦侵略军统帅古斯鲁姆的营地。

usage.note: 此处指军队驻扎过冬，非表示平静或结婚成家。
usage.example: These had settled down for the winter at Chippenham: thither Alfred went.
usage.exampleZh: 丹麦军队已在奇彭纳姆安顿下来过冬，阿尔弗雷德便前往那里。

usage.note: 引出比较对象，常作过去分词短语。
usage.example: The force there assembled was trivial compared with the Danish horde.
usage.exampleZh: 那里集结的兵力与丹麦大军相比，实在微不足道。

usage.note: be on the move 可指持续转移，也可指忙碌奔波。
usage.example: He was constantly on the move, drawing the Danes after him.
usage.exampleZh: 他不停转移，引着丹麦人追赶。

rows.en: Technology trends may push Silicon Valley back to the future.
rows.zh: 技术发展的潮流，或许会推动硅谷以回归往昔的方式走向未来。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Carver Mead, a pioneer in integrated circuits and a professor of computer science at the California Institute of Technology, notes there are now workstations that enable engineers to design, test and produce chips right on their desks, much the way an editor creates a newsletter on a Macintosh.
rows.zh: 集成电路先驱、加州理工学院计算机科学教授卡弗·米德指出，如今已有工作站让工程师直接在办公桌上设计、测试和生产芯片，大致就像编辑用麦金塔电脑制作简报一样。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: As the time and cost of making a chip drop to a few days and a few hundred dollars, engineers may soon be free to let their imaginations soar without being penalized by expensive failures.
rows.zh: 当制造一枚芯片所需的时间和费用降到几天、几百美元时，工程师或许很快就能让想象力自由驰骋，而不必因失败代价高昂而受到惩罚。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Mead predicts that inventors will be able to perfect powerful customized chips over a weekend at the office—spawning a new generation of garage start-ups and giving the U.S. a jump on its foreign rivals in getting new products to market fast.
rows.zh: 米德预言，发明者将能够利用一个周末在办公室里完善性能强大的定制芯片，从而催生新一代从车库起家的初创企业，并使美国在迅速把新产品推向市场方面领先外国对手一步。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: ‘We've got more garages with smart people,’ Mead observes.
rows.zh: 米德说：“我们有更多车库，里面有聪明人。”
rows.speaker: 米德

rows.en: ‘We really thrive on anarchy.’
rows.zh: “我们确实靠这种自由无序的环境蓬勃发展。”
rows.speaker: 米德

rows.en: And on Asians.
rows.zh: 同样也靠亚洲人。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Already, orientals and Asian Americans constitute the majority of the engineering staffs at many Valley firms.
rows.zh: 在硅谷的许多公司里，亚洲人和亚裔美国人已占工程技术人员的大多数。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: And Chinese, Korean, Filipino and Indian engineers are graduating in droves from California's colleges.
rows.zh: 而中国、韩国、菲律宾和印度背景的工程师，正一批批从加利福尼亚的大学毕业。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: As the heads of next-generation start-ups, these Asian innovators can draw on customs and languages to forge tighter links with crucial Pacific Rim markets.
rows.zh: 作为下一代初创企业的负责人，这些亚洲创新者能借助自身熟悉的习俗和语言，与至关重要的环太平洋市场建立更紧密的联系。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: For instance, Alex Au, a Stanford Ph.D. from Hong Kong, has set up a Taiwan factory to challenge Japan's near lock on the memory-chip market.
rows.zh: 例如，来自香港的斯坦福大学博士亚历克斯·欧，在台湾设立了一家工厂，挑战日本对存储芯片市场近乎垄断的地位。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: India-born N. Damodar Reddy's tiny California company reopened an AT&T chip plant in Kansas City last spring with financing from the state of Missouri.
rows.zh: 出生于印度的恩·达莫达尔·雷迪，他在加利福尼亚的小公司去年春天获得密苏里州的资金支持，使堪萨斯城一家美国电话电报公司的芯片工厂重新开工。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Before it becomes a retirement village, Silicon Valley may prove a classroom for building a global business.
rows.zh: 在变成退休者聚居区之前，硅谷或许会先成为人们学习如何创办全球企业的课堂。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: 后接动词原形，表示有自由或条件去做，而非免费。
usage.example: As the time and cost of making a chip drop to a few days and a few hundred dollars, engineers may soon be free to let their imaginations soar without being penalized by expensive failures.
usage.exampleZh: 当制造一枚芯片所需的时间和费用降到几天、几百美元时，工程师或许很快就能让想象力自由驰骋，而不必因失败代价高昂而受到惩罚。

usage.matchedForm: giving the U.S. a jump on
usage.note: a jump on someone 表示领先优势，常与 get 或 give 搭配。
usage.example: Mead predicts that inventors will be able to perfect powerful customized chips over a weekend at the office—spawning a new generation of garage start-ups and giving the U.S. a jump on its foreign rivals in getting new products to market fast.
usage.exampleZh: 米德预言，发明者将能够利用一个周末在办公室里完善性能强大的定制芯片，从而催生新一代从车库起家的初创企业，并使美国在迅速把新产品推向市场方面领先外国对手一步。

usage.note: 后接促进成长的因素，此处 anarchy 形容缺少束缚的环境。
usage.example: ‘We really thrive on anarchy.’
usage.exampleZh: “我们确实靠这种自由无序的环境蓬勃发展。”

usage.note: 常用来描述人群的大批涌入、离开或出现。
usage.example: And Chinese, Korean, Filipino and Indian engineers are graduating in droves from California's colleges.
usage.exampleZh: 而中国、韩国、菲律宾和印度背景的工程师，正一批批从加利福尼亚的大学毕业。

usage.note: 后接知识、经验或资源，强调调动已有积累。
usage.example: As the heads of next-generation start-ups, these Asian innovators can draw on customs and languages to forge tighter links with crucial Pacific Rim markets.
usage.exampleZh: 作为下一代初创企业的负责人，这些亚洲创新者能借助自身熟悉的习俗和语言，与至关重要的环太平洋市场建立更紧密的联系。

rows.en: Some old people are oppressed by the fear of death.
rows.zh: 有些老年人被死亡的恐惧所压迫。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In the young there is a justification for this feeling.
rows.zh: 年轻人有这种感受，是有道理的。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Young men who have reason to fear that they will be killed in battle may justifiably feel bitter in the thought that they have been cheated of the best things that life has to offer.
rows.zh: 有理由担心自己会战死的青年，想到人生所能给予的最美好的东西竟被夺走，自然有理由感到痛苦不平。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: But in an old man who has known human joys and sorrows, and has achieved whatever work it was in him to do, the fear of death is somewhat abject and ignoble.
rows.zh: 但是，一个已经体验过人间悲欢、完成了自己能力所及的工作的人，到了老年仍然害怕死亡，就显得有些卑怯，有失尊严了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The best way to overcome it—so at least it seems to me—is to make your interests gradually wider and more impersonal, until bit by bit the walls of the ego recede, and your life becomes increasingly merged in the universal life.
rows.zh: 克服这种恐惧的最好办法——至少在我看来如此——就是让自己的兴趣逐渐扩大，越来越超越个人，直到自我的围墙一点点退去，自己的生命越来越融入普遍的生命之中。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: An individual human existence should be like a river—small at first, narrowly contained within its banks, and rushing passionately past boulders and over waterfalls.
rows.zh: 一个人的生命应当像一条河：起初很小，紧紧局限在两岸之间，激情奔涌，冲过巨石，跌下瀑布。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Gradually the river grows wider, the banks recede, the waters flow more quietly, and in the end, without any visible break, they become merged in the sea, and painlessly lose their individual being.
rows.zh: 河流渐渐宽阔，河岸向两侧退去，水流趋于平静，最后在看不出任何断裂的情况下汇入大海，毫无痛苦地失去独立的存在。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The man who, in old age, can see his life in this way, will not suffer from the fear of death, since the things he cares for will continue.
rows.zh: 人在老年若能这样看待自己的生命，就不会受死亡恐惧的折磨，因为他关心的事物还会继续存在。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: And if, with the decay of vitality, weariness increases, the thought of rest will be not unwelcome.
rows.zh: 如果随着生命力的衰退，倦意日增，那么想到可以休息，也并非不受欢迎。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: I should wish to die while still at work, knowing that others will carry on what I can no longer do, and content in the thought that what was possible has been done.
rows.zh: 我希望去世时自己仍在工作，知道别人会继续做我再也无法做的事情，并欣慰地想到：凡是可能做到的，都已经做了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: reason 在这里通常不加冠词，后接动词原形。
usage.example: Young men who have reason to fear that they will be killed in battle may justifiably feel bitter in the thought that they have been cheated of the best things that life has to offer.
usage.exampleZh: 有理由担心自己会战死的青年，想到人生所能给予的最美好的东西竟被夺走，自然有理由感到痛苦不平。

usage.note: cheat someone of something 表示以不公的方式使其失去应得之物。
usage.example: Young men who have reason to fear that they will be killed in battle may justifiably feel bitter in the thought that they have been cheated of the best things that life has to offer.
usage.exampleZh: 有理由担心自己会战死的青年，想到人生所能给予的最美好的东西竟被夺走，自然有理由感到痛苦不平。

usage.note: 强调变化缓慢而逐步发生。
usage.example: The best way to overcome it—so at least it seems to me—is to make your interests gradually wider and more impersonal, until bit by bit the walls of the ego recede, and your life becomes increasingly merged in the universal life.
usage.exampleZh: 克服这种恐惧的最好办法——至少在我看来如此——就是让自己的兴趣逐渐扩大，越来越超越个人，直到自我的围墙一点点退去，自己的生命越来越融入普遍的生命之中。

usage.note: 后接疾病或痛苦处境，此处指受恐惧困扰。
usage.example: The man who, in old age, can see his life in this way, will not suffer from the fear of death, since the things he cares for will continue.
usage.exampleZh: 人在老年若能这样看待自己的生命，就不会受死亡恐惧的折磨，因为他关心的事物还会继续存在。

usage.note: 可接名词或动名词；此处宾语为 what 引导的从句。
usage.example: I should wish to die while still at work, knowing that others will carry on what I can no longer do, and content in the thought that what was possible has been done.
usage.exampleZh: 我希望去世时自己仍在工作，知道别人会继续做我再也无法做的事情，并欣慰地想到：凡是可能做到的，都已经做了。

rows.en: When anyone opens a current account at a bank, he is lending the bank money, repayment of which he may demand at any time, either in cash or by drawing a cheque in favour of another person.
rows.zh: 任何人在银行开立活期账户时，都等于把钱借给银行；他随时可以要求偿还，既可以取现金，也可以开一张以他人为收款人的支票。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Primarily, the banker-customer relationship is that of debtor and creditor—who is which depending on whether the customer's account is in credit or is overdrawn.
rows.zh: 银行与客户的关系，首先是债务人与债权人的关系；究竟谁是哪一方，取决于客户账户上有余额还是已经透支。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: But, in addition to that basically simple concept, the bank and its customer owe a large number of obligations to one another.
rows.zh: 但除了这一基本上很简单的概念，银行和客户还彼此承担着许多义务。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Many of these obligations can give rise to problems and complications but a bank customer, unlike, say, a buyer of goods, cannot complain that the law is loaded against him.
rows.zh: 其中许多义务可能引起问题和纠纷，不过银行客户不能像例如商品买主那样，抱怨法律偏向对方、不利于自己。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The bank must obey its customer’s instructions, and not those of anyone else.
rows.zh: 银行必须遵照客户本人的指示，而不能听从其他任何人的指示。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: When, for example, a customer first opens an account, he instructs the bank to debit his account only in respect of cheques drawn by himself.
rows.zh: 例如，客户刚开户时，会指示银行，只能凭他本人签发的支票从其账户扣款。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He gives the bank specimens of his signature, and there is a very firm rule that the bank has no right or authority to pay out a customer's money on a cheque on which its customer's signature has been forged.
rows.zh: 他向银行提供自己的签名样本；有一条非常明确的规则：如果支票上客户的签名系伪造，银行就没有权利或授权支付客户的存款。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It makes no difference that the forgery may have been a very skilful one: the bank must recognize its customer's signature.
rows.zh: 即便伪造得非常高明也没有区别：银行必须辨认得出客户的签名。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: For this reason there is no risk to the customer in the practice, adopted by banks, of printing the customer’s name on his cheques.
rows.zh: 因此，银行把客户姓名印在支票上的做法，对客户并没有风险。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: If this facilitates forgery, it is the bank which will lose, not the customer.
rows.zh: 如果这种做法使伪造变得容易，蒙受损失的是银行，而不是客户。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: 用于支票等金融文本；一般语境也可表示支持或赞成。
usage.example: When anyone opens a current account at a bank, he is lending the bank money, repayment of which he may demand at any time, either in cash or by drawing a cheque in favour of another person.
usage.exampleZh: 任何人在银行开立活期账户时，都等于把钱借给银行；他随时可以要求偿还，既可以取现金，也可以开一张以他人为收款人的支票。

usage.note: 与 overdrawn 相对，指账户中还有属于客户的可用款项。
usage.example: Primarily, the banker-customer relationship is that of debtor and creditor—who is which depending on whether the customer's account is in credit or is overdrawn.
usage.exampleZh: 银行与客户的关系，首先是债务人与债权人的关系；究竟谁是哪一方，取决于客户账户上有余额还是已经透支。

usage.note: 后接问题、变化或结果，常用于正式书面语。
usage.example: Many of these obligations can give rise to problems and complications but a bank customer, unlike, say, a buyer of goods, cannot complain that the law is loaded against him.
usage.exampleZh: 其中许多义务可能引起问题和纠纷，不过银行客户不能像例如商品买主那样，抱怨法律偏向对方、不利于自己。

usage.note: 正式表达，此处限定银行扣款所依据的支票。
usage.example: When, for example, a customer first opens an account, he instructs the bank to debit his account only in respect of cheques drawn by himself.
usage.exampleZh: 例如，客户刚开户时，会指示银行，只能凭他本人签发的支票从其账户扣款。

usage.note: 常用 it makes no difference that/whether，表示某因素不改变结论。
usage.example: It makes no difference that the forgery may have been a very skilful one: the bank must recognize its customer's signature.
usage.exampleZh: 即便伪造得非常高明也没有区别：银行必须辨认得出客户的签名。

rows.en: The deepest holes of all are made for oil, and they go down to as much as 25,000 feet.
rows.zh: 所有孔井中最深的是为开采石油而钻的，深度可达二万五千英尺。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: But we do not need to send men down to get the oil out, as we must with other mineral deposits.
rows.zh: 不过，开采石油不必像开采其他矿藏那样，把人送到地下去。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The holes are only borings, less than a foot in diameter.
rows.zh: 这些井只是钻孔，直径还不到一英尺。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: My particular experience is largely in oil, and the search for oil has done more to improve deep drilling than any other mining activity.
rows.zh: 我本人的专门经验主要在石油领域，而寻找石油对于深井钻探技术的改进，比任何其他采矿活动都贡献更大。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: When it has been decided where we are going to drill, we put up at the surface an oil derrick.
rows.zh: 一旦决定了在哪里钻探，我们便在地面架起一座石油井架。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It has to be tall because it is like a giant block and tackle, and we have to lower into the ground and haul out of the ground great lengths of drill pipe which are rotated by an engine at the top and are fitted with a cutting bit at the bottom.
rows.zh: 井架必须很高，因为它就像一个巨大的滑轮组；我们必须把很长的钻杆放进地下，再从地下吊上来，钻杆由顶部的发动机带动旋转，底端则装着切削钻头。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The geologist needs to know what rocks the drill has reached, so every so often a sample is obtained with a coring bit.
rows.zh: 地质学家需要知道钻头已钻到了什么岩石，因此每隔一段时间，就要用取芯钻头采一份样本。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It cuts a clean cylinder of rock, from which can be seen the strata the drill has been cutting through.
rows.zh: 这种钻头切下一段完整的圆柱形岩芯，从中可以看出钻头已经钻穿的地层。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Once we get down to the oil, it usually flows to the surface because great pressure, either from gas or water, is pushing it.
rows.zh: 一旦钻到石油层，石油通常会流上地面，因为有气体或水产生的巨大压力在推着它。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: This pressure must be under control, and we control it by means of the mud which we circulate down the drill pipe.
rows.zh: 这股压力必须受到控制，而我们用沿钻杆向下循环输送的泥浆来控制它。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: We endeavour to avoid the old, romantic idea of a gusher, which wastes oil and gas.
rows.zh: 我们力求避免过去那种颇具浪漫色彩的井喷，因为井喷会浪费石油和天然气。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: We want it to stay down the hole until we can lead it off in a controlled manner.
rows.zh: 我们希望让石油留在井下，直到能够以受控的方式将它引出来。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: 放在数量前强调程度或数量之大，此处修饰深度。
usage.example: The deepest holes of all are made for oil, and they go down to as much as 25,000 feet.
usage.exampleZh: 所有孔井中最深的是为开采石油而钻的，深度可达二万五千英尺。

usage.note: 此处宾语为井架，意为建起设施，不是张贴或忍受。
usage.example: When it has been decided where we are going to drill, we put up at the surface an oil derrick.
usage.exampleZh: 一旦决定了在哪里钻探，我们便在地面架起一座石油井架。

usage.note: 表示间歇重复，不必有固定频率。
usage.example: The geologist needs to know what rocks the drill has reached, so every so often a sample is obtained with a coring bit.
usage.exampleZh: 地质学家需要知道钻头已钻到了什么岩石，因此每隔一段时间，就要用取芯钻头采一份样本。

usage.note: 常与 be、keep、bring 搭配，表示局面或力量受掌控。
usage.example: This pressure must be under control, and we control it by means of the mud which we circulate down the drill pipe.
usage.exampleZh: 这股压力必须受到控制，而我们用沿钻杆向下循环输送的泥浆来控制它。

usage.note: 后接所用的工具、材料或方法。
usage.example: This pressure must be under control, and we control it by means of the mud which we circulate down the drill pipe.
usage.exampleZh: 这股压力必须受到控制，而我们用沿钻杆向下循环输送的泥浆来控制它。

rows.en: Beyond two or three days, the world’s best weather forecasts are speculative, and beyond six or seven they are worthless.
rows.zh: 即使是世界上最好的天气预报，超过两三天也只是推测，超过六七天便毫无价值。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The Butterfly Effect is the reason.
rows.zh: 原因就在于蝴蝶效应。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: For small pieces of weather — and to a global forecaster, small can mean thunderstorms and blizzards — any prediction deteriorates rapidly.
rows.zh: 对于天气中的小尺度现象——在全球天气预报者眼中，雷暴和暴风雪也可以算小——任何预测都会迅速失准。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Errors and uncertainties multiply, cascading upward through a chain of turbulent features, from dust devils and squalls up to continent-size eddies that only satellites can see.
rows.zh: 误差与不确定性不断倍增，沿着一连串湍流现象逐级向更大尺度传递，从尘卷风和飑，一直到只有卫星才能观测到的大陆尺度涡旋。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The modern weather models work with a grid of points of the order of sixty miles apart, and even so, some starting data has to be guessed, since ground stations and satellites cannot see everywhere.
rows.zh: 现代天气模型使用的网格，各点相隔约六十英里；即便如此，有些初始数据仍得靠估计，因为地面观测站和卫星不可能看遍每一处。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: But suppose the earth could be covered with sensors spaced one foot apart, rising at one-foot intervals all the way to the top of the atmosphere.
rows.zh: 不过，假设整个地球都能布满间距一英尺的传感器，并且以一英尺的垂直间隔，一直布设到大气层顶端。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Suppose every sensor gives perfectly accurate readings of temperature, pressure, humidity, and any other quantity a meteorologist would want.
rows.zh: 再假设每个传感器都能完全准确地测出温度、气压、湿度，以及气象学家想要的任何其他量。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Precisely at noon an infinitely powerful computer takes all the data and calculates what will happen at each point at 12.01, then 12.02, then 12.03...
rows.zh: 正午十二点整，一台运算能力无限强大的计算机收集全部数据，算出十二点零一分每一点会出现什么情况，接着算十二点零二分、十二点零三分……
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The computer will still be unable to predict whether Princeton, New Jersey, will have sun or rain on a day one month away.
rows.zh: 这台计算机仍然无法预测，一个月后的某一天，新泽西州普林斯顿究竟是晴天还是雨天。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: At noon the spaces between the sensors will hide fluctuations that the computer will not know about, tiny deviations from the average.
rows.zh: 正午时，传感器之间的空隙中隐藏着计算机无法得知的起伏，也就是偏离平均值的微小波动。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: By 12.01, those fluctuations will already have created small errors one foot away.
rows.zh: 到了十二点零一分，这些起伏就已经在一英尺之外造成了小误差。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Soon the errors will have multiplied to the ten-foot scale, and so on up to the size of the globe.
rows.zh: 很快，误差就会扩大到十英尺的尺度，然后这样不断扩大，直至遍及整个地球。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: 强调环节相互关联，而非毫无联系地并列。
usage.example: Errors and uncertainties multiply, cascading upward through a chain of turbulent features, from dust devils and squalls up to continent-size eddies that only satellites can see.
usage.exampleZh: 误差与不确定性不断倍增，沿着一连串湍流现象逐级向更大尺度传递，从尘卷风和飑，一直到只有卫星才能观测到的大陆尺度涡旋。

usage.note: 用于科学或技术语境，表示近似的数量或尺度。
usage.example: The modern weather models work with a grid of points of the order of sixty miles apart, and even so, some starting data has to be guessed, since ground stations and satellites cannot see everywhere.
usage.exampleZh: 现代天气模型使用的网格，各点相隔约六十英里；即便如此，有些初始数据仍得靠估计，因为地面观测站和卫星不可能看遍每一处。

usage.note: 强调空间上延伸到某个终点，也可用于过程。
usage.example: But suppose the earth could be covered with sensors spaced one foot apart, rising at one-foot intervals all the way to the top of the atmosphere.
usage.exampleZh: 不过，假设整个地球都能布满间距一英尺的传感器，并且以一英尺的垂直间隔，一直布设到大气层顶端。

usage.note: 后接动词原形，表示能力或条件不足以完成某事。
usage.example: The computer will still be unable to predict whether Princeton, New Jersey, will have sun or rain on a day one month away.
usage.exampleZh: 这台计算机仍然无法预测，一个月后的某一天，新泽西州普林斯顿究竟是晴天还是雨天。

usage.note: 表示前述规律或列举还会延续；此处是误差继续扩散。
usage.example: Soon the errors will have multiplied to the ten-foot scale, and so on up to the size of the globe.
usage.exampleZh: 很快，误差就会扩大到十英尺的尺度，然后这样不断扩大，直至遍及整个地球。

rows.en: Two factors weigh heavily against the effectiveness of scientific research in industry.
rows.zh: 有两个因素严重妨碍工业科研发挥成效。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: One is the general atmosphere of secrecy in which it is carried out, the other the lack of freedom of the individual research worker.
rows.zh: 一是科研工作普遍在保密气氛下进行，二是科研人员个人缺乏自由。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In so far as any inquiry is a secret one, it naturally limits all those engaged in carrying it out from effective contact with their fellow scientists either in other countries or in universities, or even, often enough, in other departments of the same firm.
rows.zh: 只要一项研究具有保密性质，自然就会限制所有参与者与同行进行有效交流，不论这些同行是在别国、大学，甚至往往就在同一公司的其他部门。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The degree of secrecy naturally varies considerably.
rows.zh: 保密程度自然有很大差别。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Some of the bigger firms are engaged in researches which are of such general and fundamental nature that it is a positive advantage to them not to keep them secret.
rows.zh: 有些大公司进行的研究如此广泛而基础，以至于不予保密反而会给它们带来实实在在的好处。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Yet a great many processes depending on such research are sought for with complete secrecy until the stage at which patents can be taken out.
rows.zh: 不过，以这类研究为基础的许多工艺，其开发仍完全保密，直至达到能够申请专利的阶段。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Even more processes are never patented at all but kept as secret processes.
rows.zh: 还有更多工艺根本不申请专利，而是作为秘密工艺保留下来。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: This applies particularly to chemical industries, where chance discoveries play a much larger part than they do in physical and mechanical industries.
rows.zh: 化学工业尤其如此，因为偶然发现所起的作用，比在物理和机械工业中大得多。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Sometimes the secrecy goes to such an extent that the whole nature of the research cannot be mentioned.
rows.zh: 有时保密竟到了这种地步：连研究本身的性质都不能提及。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Many firms, for instance, have great difficulty in obtaining technical or scientific books from libraries because they are unwilling to have their names entered as having taken out such and such a book, for fear the agents of other firms should be able to trace the kind of research they are likely to be undertaking.
rows.zh: 例如，许多公司从图书馆借取技术或科学书籍都非常困难，因为它们不愿留下借过某某书的公司名称记录，唯恐其他公司的探子据此追查出它们可能正在进行哪类研究。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: weigh against 表示构成不利因素，heavily 加重影响程度。
usage.example: Two factors weigh heavily against the effectiveness of scientific research in industry.
usage.exampleZh: 有两个因素严重妨碍工业科研发挥成效。

usage.note: 限定论述成立的条件或程度，此处指研究具有保密性质这一点。
usage.example: In so far as any inquiry is a secret one, it naturally limits all those engaged in carrying it out from effective contact with their fellow scientists either in other countries or in universities, or even, often enough, in other departments of the same firm.
usage.exampleZh: 只要一项研究具有保密性质，自然就会限制所有参与者与同行进行有效交流，不论这些同行是在别国、大学，甚至往往就在同一公司的其他部门。

usage.note: take out 可搭配 patent、insurance 等，表示办理或取得正式权利。
usage.example: Yet a great many processes depending on such research are sought for with complete secrecy until the stage at which patents can be taken out.
usage.exampleZh: 不过，以这类研究为基础的许多工艺，其开发仍完全保密，直至达到能够申请专利的阶段。

usage.note: 常与 that 结果从句连用，说明做法发展到某种极端程度。
usage.example: Sometimes the secrecy goes to such an extent that the whole nature of the research cannot be mentioned.
usage.exampleZh: 有时保密竟到了这种地步：连研究本身的性质都不能提及。

usage.note: 后可接 that 从句；原文省略 that，并用 should 表示所担心的可能。
usage.example: Many firms, for instance, have great difficulty in obtaining technical or scientific books from libraries because they are unwilling to have their names entered as having taken out such and such a book, for fear the agents of other firms should be able to trace the kind of research they are likely to be undertaking.
usage.exampleZh: 例如，许多公司从图书馆借取技术或科学书籍都非常困难，因为它们不愿留下借过某某书的公司名称记录，唯恐其他公司的探子据此追查出它们可能正在进行哪类研究。

usage.note: at all 在否定句中加强否定；本句由 never 提供否定，意为从来不申请专利。
usage.example: Even more processes are never patented at all but kept as secret processes.
usage.exampleZh: 还有更多工艺根本不申请专利，而是作为秘密工艺保留下来。

rows.en: In the organization of industrial life the influence of the factory upon the physiological and mental state of the workers has been completely neglected.
rows.zh: 在组织工业生活时，工厂对工人生理与心理状态的影响一直完全遭到忽视。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Modern industry is based on the conception of the maximum production at lowest cost, in order that an individual or a group of individuals may earn as much money as possible.
rows.zh: 现代工业立足于以最低成本获得最大产量的观念，目的是让个人或某个群体赚到尽可能多的钱。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It has expanded without any idea of the true nature of the human beings who run the machines, and without giving any consideration to the effects produced on the individuals and on their descendants by the artificial mode of existence imposed by the factory.
rows.zh: 它的发展既没有认识操作机器者的真实人性，也完全没有考虑工厂强加的这种人为生活方式，会对个人及其后代产生什么影响。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The great cities have been built with no regard for us.
rows.zh: 大城市的建造丝毫没有顾及我们。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The shape and dimensions of the skyscrapers depend entirely on the necessity of obtaining the maximum income per square foot of ground, and of offering to the tenants offices and apartments that please them.
rows.zh: 摩天楼的形状和尺寸，完全取决于两种需要：让每平方英尺土地带来最大收入，以及为租户提供使他们满意的办公室和公寓。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: This caused the construction of gigantic buildings where too large masses of human beings are crowded together.
rows.zh: 这就造成了庞大建筑的兴建，里面挤着过于密集的人群。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Civilized men like such a way of living.
rows.zh: 文明社会的人们喜欢这样的生活方式。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: While they enjoy the comfort and banal luxury of their dwelling, they do not realize that they are deprived of the necessities of life.
rows.zh: 他们享受住所的舒适和庸俗的奢华，却没有意识到自己被剥夺了生活中必不可少的东西。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The modern city consists of monstrous edifices and of dark, narrow streets full of petrol fumes and toxic gases, torn by the noise of the taxicabs, lorries and buses, and thronged ceaselessly by great crowds.
rows.zh: 现代城市由巨兽般的建筑物和阴暗狭窄的街道构成；街上充满汽油烟气和有毒气体，出租车、卡车和公共汽车的噪声刺耳不断，拥挤的人潮川流不息。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Obviously, it has not been planned for the good of its inhabitants.
rows.zh: 显然，这样的城市并非为居民的福祉而规划。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: 常用被动结构，指出制度、观点或行动的依据。
usage.example: Modern industry is based on the conception of the maximum production at lowest cost, in order that an individual or a group of individuals may earn as much money as possible.
usage.exampleZh: 现代工业立足于以最低成本获得最大产量的观念，目的是让个人或某个群体赚到尽可能多的钱。

usage.note: regard for 表示对某人或其利益的重视；no 加强否定。
usage.example: The great cities have been built with no regard for us.
usage.exampleZh: 大城市的建造丝毫没有顾及我们。

usage.note: deprive someone of something 的被动式，of 后接被夺去的东西。
usage.example: While they enjoy the comfort and banal luxury of their dwelling, they do not realize that they are deprived of the necessities of life.
usage.exampleZh: 他们享受住所的舒适和庸俗的奢华，却没有意识到自己被剥夺了生活中必不可少的东西。

usage.note: 主语是整体，of 后列出组成部分，一般不用被动语态。
usage.example: The modern city consists of monstrous edifices and of dark, narrow streets full of petrol fumes and toxic gases, torn by the noise of the taxicabs, lorries and buses, and thronged ceaselessly by great crowds.
usage.exampleZh: 现代城市由巨兽般的建筑物和阴暗狭窄的街道构成；街上充满汽油烟气和有毒气体，出租车、卡车和公共汽车的噪声刺耳不断，拥挤的人潮川流不息。

usage.note: good 在此作名词，表示福祉或益处。
usage.example: Obviously, it has not been planned for the good of its inhabitants.
usage.exampleZh: 显然，这样的城市并非为居民的福祉而规划。

rows.en: In the early days of the settlement of Australia, enterprising settlers unwisely introduced the European rabbit.
rows.zh: 在澳大利亚殖民定居的早期，有些富于进取心的定居者做了一件不明智的事：引进欧洲兔。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: This rabbit had no natural enemies in the Antipodes, so that it multiplied with that promiscuous abandon characteristic of rabbits.
rows.zh: 这种兔子在南半球这片土地上没有天敌，便以兔类特有的那种毫无节制的滥交方式大肆繁殖。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It overran a whole continent.
rows.zh: 它们泛滥了整个大陆。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It caused devastation by burrowing and by devouring the herbage which might have maintained millions of sheep and cattle.
rows.zh: 它们挖洞，又吃掉本可养活数百万只牛羊的牧草，造成严重破坏。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Scientists discovered that this particular variety of rabbit (and apparently no other animal) was susceptible to a fatal virus disease, myxomatosis.
rows.zh: 科学家发现，这一种兔子——而且看来没有别的动物——很容易感染一种致命的病毒病：黏液瘤病。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: By infecting animals and letting them loose in the burrows, local epidemics of this disease could be created.
rows.zh: 把动物感染后放入兔穴，就能在局部造成这种疾病的流行。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Later it was found that there was a type of mosquito which acted as the carrier of this disease and passed it on to the rabbits.
rows.zh: 后来人们发现，有一种蚊子能携带这种病，并把它传给兔子。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: So while the rest of the world was trying to get rid of mosquitoes, Australia was encouraging this one.
rows.zh: 于是，世界其他地方都在努力消灭蚊子时，澳大利亚却在鼓励这种蚊子繁殖。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It effectively spread the disease all over the continent and drastically reduced the rabbit population.
rows.zh: 它有效地把疾病传播到整个大陆，使兔子的数量大幅减少。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It later became apparent that rabbits were developing a degree of resistance to this disease, so that the rabbit population was unlikely to be completely exterminated.
rows.zh: 后来，人们逐渐发现兔子正在对这种病产生一定抵抗力，因此不大可能把兔群彻底消灭。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: There were hopes, however, that the problem of the rabbit would become manageable.
rows.zh: 不过，人们仍希望兔患能变得可控制。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Ironically, Europe, which had bequeathed the rabbit as a pest to Australia, acquired this man-made disease as a pestilence.
rows.zh: 具有讽刺意味的是，原先把兔子这一祸害送给澳大利亚的欧洲，自己却遭受了这种人为传播疾病的瘟疫之灾。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: A French physician decided to get rid of the wild rabbits on his own estate and introduced myxomatosis.
rows.zh: 一位法国医生决定清除自己庄园上的野兔，便引入了黏液瘤病。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It did not, however, remain within the confines of his estate.
rows.zh: 然而，疾病并没有局限在他的庄园之内。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It spread through France, where wild rabbits are not generally regarded as a pest but as a sport and a useful food supply, and it spread to Britain where wild rabbits are regarded as a pest but where domesticated rabbits, equally susceptible to the disease, are the basis of a profitable fur industry.
rows.zh: 它蔓延到法国各地；在那里，野兔一般不被看作害兽，而被视为狩猎对象和一种有用的食物来源；疾病还传到了英国，那里虽把野兔视为害兽，但同样容易染病的家兔却是利润可观的毛皮业的基础。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The question became one of whether Man could control the disease he had invented.
rows.zh: 问题于是变成：人类究竟能不能控制自己制造出来的疾病。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: to 为介词，可接疾病或影响；此处讲动物对病毒病的易感性。
usage.example: Scientists discovered that this particular variety of rabbit (and apparently no other animal) was susceptible to a fatal virus disease, myxomatosis.
usage.exampleZh: 科学家发现，这一种兔子——而且看来没有别的动物——很容易感染一种致命的病毒病：黏液瘤病。

usage.note: let 后接宾语和形容词 loose；此处指放回兔穴。
usage.example: By infecting animals and letting them loose in the burrows, local epidemics of this disease could be created.
usage.exampleZh: 把动物感染后放入兔穴，就能在局部造成这种疾病的流行。

usage.note: 代词宾语放在 pass 与 on 之间；此处传递的是疾病。
usage.example: Later it was found that there was a type of mosquito which acted as the carrier of this disease and passed it on to the rabbits.
usage.exampleZh: 后来人们发现，有一种蚊子能携带这种病，并把它传给兔子。

usage.note: 后接不想保留的人或事物，此处表示消灭蚊子。
usage.example: So while the rest of the world was trying to get rid of mosquitoes, Australia was encouraging this one.
usage.exampleZh: 于是，世界其他地方都在努力消灭蚊子时，澳大利亚却在鼓励这种蚊子繁殖。

usage.note: confines 常用复数，指界限；可描述具体疆界或抽象范围。
usage.example: It did not, however, remain within the confines of his estate.
usage.exampleZh: 然而，疾病并没有局限在他的庄园之内。

rows.en: There has long been a superstition among mariners that porpoises will save drowning men by pushing them to the surface, or protect them from sharks by surrounding them in defensive formation.
rows.zh: 水手们长期以来有一种迷信，认为鼠海豚会把溺水的人推到水面上救活，或围成防御阵形，保护他们免受鲨鱼袭击。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Marine Studio biologists have pointed out that, however intelligent they may be, it is probably a mistake to credit dolphins with any motive of lifesaving.
rows.zh: 海洋摄影场的生物学家指出，不管海豚多么聪明，认为它们具有救人的动机，大概都是误解。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: On the occasions when they have pushed to shore an unconscious human being they have much more likely done it out of curiosity or for sport, as in riding the bow waves of a ship.
rows.zh: 它们有时把失去知觉的人推到岸边，更可能是出于好奇或为了玩耍，就像它们追逐船首的波浪一样。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In 1928 some porpoises were photographed working like beavers to push ashore a waterlogged mattress.
rows.zh: 一九二八年，有人拍到几只鼠海豚拼命把一张浸透水的床垫推上岸。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: If, as has been reported, they have protected humans from sharks, it may have been because curiosity attracted them and because the scent of a possible meal attracted the sharks.
rows.zh: 如果它们确实像报道所说的那样保护过人类，使人免遭鲨鱼袭击，那么可能是好奇心吸引了它们，而潜在猎物的气味又引来了鲨鱼。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Porpoises and sharks are natural enemies.
rows.zh: 鼠海豚和鲨鱼是天敌。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It is possible that upon such an occasion a battle ensued, with the sharks being driven away or killed.
rows.zh: 在这种场合下，也许发生了一场搏斗，鲨鱼被赶走或杀死了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Whether it be bird, fish or beast, the porpoise is intrigued with anything that is alive.
rows.zh: 不论是鸟、鱼还是兽，鼠海豚对任何活物都感兴趣。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: They are constantly after the turtles, who peacefully submit to all sorts of indignities.
rows.zh: 它们总是追着海龟不放，而海龟对各种欺负都温顺地忍受。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: One young calf especially enjoyed raising a turtle to the surface with his snout and then shoving him across the tank like an aquaplane.
rows.zh: 一只幼豚尤其喜欢用吻部把海龟顶到水面，然后像推滑水板一样推着它横过水池。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Almost any day a young porpoise may be seen trying to turn a 300-pound sea turtle over by sticking his snout under the edge of his shell and pushing up for dear life.
rows.zh: 几乎每天都能看到幼豚把吻部伸到一只三百磅重的海龟的甲壳边缘下面，拼命往上顶，想把海龟翻过来。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: This is not easy, and may require two porpoises working together.
rows.zh: 这并不容易，可能需要两只鼠海豚一起干。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In another game, as the turtle swims across the oceanarium, the first porpoise swoops down from above and butts his shell with his belly.
rows.zh: 另一种游戏是，海龟游过海洋水族馆的水池时，第一只鼠海豚从上方向下猛冲，用肚子撞它的甲壳。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: This knocks the turtle down several feet.
rows.zh: 这一撞就把海龟撞沉好几英尺。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He no sooner recovers his equilibrium than the next porpoise comes along and hits him another crack.
rows.zh: 它刚刚恢复平衡，下一只鼠海豚就过来再撞它一下。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Eventually the turtle has been butted all the way down to the floor of the tank.
rows.zh: 最后，海龟就这样一路被撞到池底。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He is now satisfied merely to try to stand up, but as soon as he does so a porpoise knocks him flat.
rows.zh: 这时它只求能站起来，但它一站起来，就有一只鼠海豚把它撞得平躺下去。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The turtle at last gives up by pulling his feet under his shell and the game is over.
rows.zh: 海龟终于把脚缩进甲壳，认了输，游戏也就结束了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: credit someone with a quality/motive 是把某种品质或动机归于某人。
usage.example: Marine Studio biologists have pointed out that, however intelligent they may be, it is probably a mistake to credit dolphins with any motive of lifesaving.
usage.exampleZh: 海洋摄影场的生物学家指出，不管海豚多么聪明，认为它们具有救人的动机，大概都是误解。

usage.note: out of 加感情或动机名词，说明行为的驱动力。
usage.example: On the occasions when they have pushed to shore an unconscious human being they have much more likely done it out of curiosity or for sport, as in riding the bow waves of a ship.
usage.exampleZh: 它们有时把失去知觉的人推到岸边，更可能是出于好奇或为了玩耍，就像它们追逐船首的波浪一样。

usage.note: to 为介词，后接不得不接受的待遇、权威等。
usage.example: They are constantly after the turtles, who peacefully submit to all sorts of indignities.
usage.exampleZh: 它们总是追着海龟不放，而海龟对各种欺负都温顺地忍受。

usage.note: 表示用尽力气，未必真的处在生命危险之中。
usage.example: Almost any day a young porpoise may be seen trying to turn a 300-pound sea turtle over by sticking his snout under the edge of his shell and pushing up for dear life.
usage.exampleZh: 几乎每天都能看到幼豚把吻部伸到一只三百磅重的海龟的甲壳边缘下面，拼命往上顶，想把海龟翻过来。

usage.matchedForm: no sooner recovers his equilibrium than
usage.note: 用于强调两事紧接着发生；no sooner 放句首时通常需要倒装。
usage.example: He no sooner recovers his equilibrium than the next porpoise comes along and hits him another crack.
usage.exampleZh: 它刚刚恢复平衡，下一只鼠海豚就过来再撞它一下。

rows.en: It is fairly clear that the sleeping period must have some function, and because there is so much of it the function would seem to be important.
rows.zh: 睡眠这段时间必定有某种功能，这一点相当清楚；而且它占据的时间如此之多，这种功能似乎应当很重要。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Speculations about its nature have been going on for literally thousands of years, and one odd finding that makes the problem puzzling is that it looks very much as if sleeping is not simply a matter of giving the body a rest.
rows.zh: 关于它究竟有何功能，人们确实已猜测了数千年；有一个奇特的发现使问题令人困惑：睡眠看来很可能不只是让身体休息那么简单。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: ‘Rest’, in terms of muscle relaxation and so on, can be achieved by a brief period lying, or even sitting down.
rows.zh: 从肌肉放松等意义上说，只要躺一小会儿，甚至坐一会儿，就能得到“休息”。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The body's tissues are self-repairing and self-restoring to a degree, and function best when more or less continuously active.
rows.zh: 身体组织在一定程度上能自行修复、自行恢复，而且在差不多持续活动时运转得最好。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In fact a basic amount of movement occurs during sleep which is specifically concerned with preventing muscle inactivity.
rows.zh: 事实上，睡眠中也存在一定的基本活动，这些活动正是为了防止肌肉处于不活动的状态。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: If it is not a question of resting the body, then perhaps it is the brain that needs resting?
rows.zh: 如果睡眠不是为了让身体休息，那么也许是大脑需要休息？
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: This might be a plausible hypothesis were it not for two factors.
rows.zh: 若非有两个因素，这倒可能是个说得通的假说。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: First the electroencephalograph (which is simply a device for recording the electrical activity of the brain by attaching electrodes to the scalp) shows that while there is a change in the pattern of activity during sleep, there is no evidence that the total amount of activity is any less.
rows.zh: 首先，脑电图仪——不过是一种把电极贴在头皮上来记录脑部电活动的装置——表明，睡眠时脑部活动的模式虽然有变化，却没有证据说明其活动总量有所减少。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The second factor is more interesting and more fundamental.
rows.zh: 第二个因素更有趣，也更根本。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Some years ago an American psychiatrist named William Dement published experiments dealing with the recording of eye-movements during sleep.
rows.zh: 几年前，一位名叫威廉·德门特的美国精神科医生公布了一些记录睡眠期间眼球运动的实验。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He showed that the average individual's sleep cycle is punctuated with peculiar bursts of eye-movements, some drifting and slow, others jerky and rapid.
rows.zh: 他证明，一般人的睡眠周期会不时插入一阵阵奇特的眼球运动，有的缓慢游移，有的急促跳动。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: People woken during these periods of eye-movements generally reported that they had been dreaming.
rows.zh: 在这些眼球运动时段被叫醒的人，通常报告说自己刚才正在做梦。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: When woken at other times they reported no dreams.
rows.zh: 在其他时间被叫醒的人则报告说没有做梦。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: If one group of people were disturbed from their eye-movement sleep for several nights on end, and another group were disturbed for an equal period of time but when they were not exhibiting eye-movements, the first group began to show some personality disorders while the others seemed more or less unaffected.
rows.zh: 如果连续几个晚上都在一组人出现眼球运动的睡眠阶段干扰他们，而对另一组人也干扰同样长的时间，却选在他们没有眼球运动时进行，那么第一组人就开始出现某些人格方面的失常，另一组人则似乎大体不受影响。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The implications of all this were that it was not the disturbance of sleep that mattered, but the disturbance of dreaming.
rows.zh: 这一切所暗示的是，真正要紧的不是睡眠受到干扰，而是做梦受到干扰。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: a matter of 后接名词或动名词，用于界定事情的性质。
usage.example: Speculations about its nature have been going on for literally thousands of years, and one odd finding that makes the problem puzzling is that it looks very much as if sleeping is not simply a matter of giving the body a rest.
usage.exampleZh: 关于它究竟有何功能，人们确实已猜测了数千年；有一个奇特的发现使问题令人困惑：睡眠看来很可能不只是让身体休息那么简单。

usage.note: 用来说明衡量或理解事物的角度。
usage.example: ‘Rest’, in terms of muscle relaxation and so on, can be achieved by a brief period lying, or even sitting down.
usage.exampleZh: 从肌肉放松等意义上说，只要躺一小会儿，甚至坐一会儿，就能得到“休息”。

usage.note: 限制判断的强度，避免被理解为完全如此。
usage.example: The body's tissues are self-repairing and self-restoring to a degree, and function best when more or less continuously active.
usage.exampleZh: 身体组织在一定程度上能自行修复、自行恢复，而且在差不多持续活动时运转得最好。

usage.note: if it were not for 的倒装形式，表达与现实相反的假设。
usage.example: This might be a plausible hypothesis were it not for two factors.
usage.exampleZh: 若非有两个因素，这倒可能是个说得通的假说。

usage.note: 接在时间段之后，如 several nights on end，强调不间断地持续。
usage.example: If one group of people were disturbed from their eye-movement sleep for several nights on end, and another group were disturbed for an equal period of time but when they were not exhibiting eye-movements, the first group began to show some personality disorders while the others seemed more or less unaffected.
usage.exampleZh: 如果连续几个晚上都在一组人出现眼球运动的睡眠阶段干扰他们，而对另一组人也干扰同样长的时间，却选在他们没有眼球运动时进行，那么第一组人就开始出现某些人格方面的失常，另一组人则似乎大体不受影响。

rows.en: How it came about that snakes manufactured poison is a mystery.
rows.zh: 蛇究竟是怎样产生毒液的，至今是个谜。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Over the periods their saliva, a mild, digestive juice like our own, was converted into a poison that defies analysis even today.
rows.zh: 在漫长岁月中，它们原本像我们的唾液一样温和、用于消化的唾液，变成了一种直到今天仍难以分析清楚的毒液。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It was not forced upon them by the survival competition; they could have caught and lived on prey without using poison, just as the thousands of non-poisonous snakes still do.
rows.zh: 这并不是生存竞争逼迫它们获得的本领；它们本来完全可以不用毒液就捕获猎物并以之为生，正如成千上万条无毒蛇如今仍在做的那样。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Poison to a snake is merely a luxury; it enables it to get its food with very little effort, no more effort than one bite.
rows.zh: 对蛇来说，毒液不过是一件奢侈品；它使蛇几乎不费力就能获得食物，所费的力气不过是咬上一口。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: And why only snakes?
rows.zh: 而为什么偏偏只有蛇呢？
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Cats, for instance, would be greatly helped; no running fights with large, fierce rats or tussles with grown rabbits—just a bite and no more effort needed.
rows.zh: 例如，猫若有毒液会大为受益；不必边跑边与凶猛的大老鼠搏斗，也不必跟成年兔子厮打，只需咬一口，再不必费劲。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In fact, it would be an assistance to all carnivores though it would be a two-edged weapon when they fought each other.
rows.zh: 事实上，所有食肉动物若有毒液都会受益，不过它们互相争斗时，这又会成为一件双刃武器。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: But, of the vertebrates, unpredictable Nature selected only snakes (and one lizard).
rows.zh: 但在脊椎动物中，变幻莫测的大自然偏偏只选择了蛇（还有一种蜥蜴）。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: One wonders also why Nature, with some snakes, concocted poison of such extreme potency.
rows.zh: 人们也不禁奇怪，大自然为什么在某些蛇身上调制出了如此剧烈的毒液。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In the conversion of saliva into poison, one might suppose that a fixed process took place.
rows.zh: 人们可能以为，唾液转变为毒液遵循的是某种固定过程。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It did not; some snakes manufactured a poison different in every respect from that of others, as different as arsenic is from strychnine, and having different effects.
rows.zh: 其实不然；有些蛇产生的毒液与其他蛇的毒液在各方面都不同，就像砒霜和士的宁截然不同一样，其作用也不同。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: One poison acts on the nerves, the other on the blood.
rows.zh: 一种毒液作用于神经，另一种则作用于血液。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The makers of the nerve poison include the mambas and the cobras and their venom is called neurotoxic.
rows.zh: 产生神经毒液的蛇包括曼巴蛇和眼镜蛇，它们的毒液称为神经毒素。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Vipers (adders) and rattlesnakes manufacture the blood poison, which is known as haemolytic.
rows.zh: 蝰蛇（蝮蛇）和响尾蛇产生的是血液毒液，称为溶血性毒液。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Both poisons are unpleasant, but by far the more unpleasant is the blood poison.
rows.zh: 两种毒液都令人难受，但血液毒液要可怕得多。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It is said that the nerve poison is the more primitive of the two, that the blood poison is, so to speak, a newer product from an improved formula.
rows.zh: 据说两者之中神经毒液比较原始，而血液毒液可以说是一种采用改良配方制出的较新产品。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Be that as it may, the nerve poison does its business with man far more quickly than the blood poison.
rows.zh: 不论事实如何，神经毒液在人身上发挥作用，比血液毒液快得多。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: This, however, means nothing.
rows.zh: 不过，这一点并不能说明什么。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Snakes did not acquire their poison for use against man but for use against prey such as rats and mice, and the effects on these of viperine poison is almost immediate.
rows.zh: 蛇获得毒液并不是为了对付人，而是为了对付大鼠、小鼠之类的猎物；蝰蛇毒液对这些动物几乎立刻就会起作用。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: 常问 how something came about，探究某种结果如何形成。
usage.example: How it came about that snakes manufactured poison is a mystery.
usage.exampleZh: 蛇究竟是怎样产生毒液的，至今是个谜。

usage.note: on 后接食物或生活来源；此处不是继续活下去之意。
usage.example: It was not forced upon them by the survival competition; they could have caught and lived on prey without using poison, just as the thousands of non-poisonous snakes still do.
usage.exampleZh: 这并不是生存竞争逼迫它们获得的本领；它们本来完全可以不用毒液就捕获猎物并以之为生，正如成千上万条无毒蛇如今仍在做的那样。

usage.note: respect 在此指方面，常与 different、similar 等形容词搭配。
usage.example: It did not; some snakes manufactured a poison different in every respect from that of others, as different as arsenic is from strychnine, and having different effects.
usage.exampleZh: 其实不然；有些蛇产生的毒液与其他蛇的毒液在各方面都不同，就像砒霜和士的宁截然不同一样，其作用也不同。

usage.note: 标示接下来的措辞并非严格字面意义，常用于比喻。
usage.example: It is said that the nerve poison is the more primitive of the two, that the blood poison is, so to speak, a newer product from an improved formula.
usage.exampleZh: 据说两者之中神经毒液比较原始，而血液毒液可以说是一种采用改良配方制出的较新产品。

usage.meaning: 即便如此；不论事实如何
usage.note: 让步性的固定说法，表示暂不争论前述说法，转谈另一点。
usage.example: Be that as it may, the nerve poison does its business with man far more quickly than the blood poison.
usage.exampleZh: 不论事实如何，神经毒液在人身上发挥作用，比血液毒液快得多。

lessons.title: William S. Hart and the early ‘Western’ film

rows.en: William S. Hart was, perhaps, the greatest of all Western stars, for unlike Gary Cooper and John Wayne he appeared in nothing but Westerns.
rows.zh: 威廉·S.哈特也许是所有西部片明星中最杰出的一位，因为他与加里·库珀和约翰·韦恩不同，出演的全都是西部片。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: From 1914 to 1924 he was supreme and unchallenged.
rows.zh: 从一九一四年到一九二四年，他的地位至高无上，无人能挑战。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It was Hart who created the basic formula of the Western film, and devised the protagonist he played in every film he made, the good-bad man, the accidental-noble outlaw, or the honest-but-framed cowboy, or the sheriff made suspect by vicious gossip; in short, the individual in conflict with himself and his frontier environment.
rows.zh: 正是哈特创造了西部片的基本模式，并设计出他在自己每一部影片中扮演的主角：亦正亦邪的人物、本性高尚却因意外境遇沦为逃犯的人、诚实却遭人陷害的牛仔，或因恶毒流言而受到怀疑的治安官；总之，是一个既与自己冲突、又与边疆环境冲突的人。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Unlike most of his contemporaries in Hollywood, Hart actually knew something of the old West.
rows.zh: 哈特与好莱坞同时代的大多数人不同，他确实了解一些昔日的西部。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He had lived in it as a child when it was already disappearing, and his hero was firmly rooted in his memories and experiences, and in both the history and the mythology of the vanished frontier.
rows.zh: 他小时候曾住在那里，而那时旧西部就已经在消失；他塑造的英雄牢牢扎根于自己的记忆和经历，也扎根于那片已经消逝的边疆的历史和传说。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: And although no period or place in American history has been more absurdly romanticized, myth and reality did join hands in at least one arena, the conflict between the individual and encroaching civilization.
rows.zh: 美国历史上没有哪个时代、哪个地方曾被如此荒唐地浪漫化；然而，神话和现实至少在一个领域确实携起了手，那就是个人与不断推进的文明之间的冲突。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Men accustomed to struggling for survival against the elements and Indians were bewildered by politicians, bankers and businessmen, and unhorsed by fences, laws and alien taboos.
rows.zh: 那些习惯于同自然力量和印第安人搏斗以求生存的男子，面对政客、银行家和商人却感到茫然，又被围栏、法律和陌生的禁忌打落马下。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Hart’s good-bad man was always an outsider, always one of the disinherited, and if he found it necessary to shoot a sheriff or rob a bank along the way, his early audiences found it easy to understand and forgive, especially when it was Hart who, in the end, overcame the attacking Indians.
rows.zh: 哈特扮演的亦正亦邪者总是局外人，总是被剥夺了应有权利的那群人之一；如果他一路上觉得非枪杀一个治安官或抢劫一家银行不可，早期观众也很容易理解并宽恕他，尤其是当最终击退来袭印第安人的正是哈特时。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Audiences in the second decade of the twentieth century found it pleasant to escape to a time when life, though hard, was relatively simple.
rows.zh: 二十世纪第二个十年间的观众，觉得逃回那个生活虽苦却相对简单的时代，是一种享受。
