rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: We still do; living in a world in which undeclared aggression, war, hypocrisy, chicanery, anarchy and impending immolation are part of our daily lives, we all want a code to live by.
rows.zh: 我们现在仍然如此；在我们生活的世界里，不宣而行的侵略、战争、虚伪、欺诈、无政府状态和迫近的毁灭，已是日常生活的一部分，所以我们都想要一套可以遵循的行为准则。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: 常表示仅限某类事物，此处强调他只演西部片。
usage.example: William S. Hart was, perhaps, the greatest of all Western stars, for unlike Gary Cooper and John Wayne he appeared in nothing but Westerns.
usage.exampleZh: 威廉·S.哈特也许是所有西部片明星中最杰出的一位，因为他与加里·库珀和约翰·韦恩不同，出演的全都是西部片。

usage.note: 既可指内心矛盾，也可指与外界不相容。
usage.example: It was Hart who created the basic formula of the Western film, and devised the protagonist he played in every film he made, the good-bad man, the accidental-noble outlaw, or the honest-but-framed cowboy, or the sheriff made suspect by vicious gossip; in short, the individual in conflict with himself and his frontier environment.
usage.exampleZh: 正是哈特创造了西部片的基本模式，并设计出他在自己每一部影片中扮演的主角：亦正亦邪的人物、本性高尚却因意外境遇沦为逃犯的人、诚实却遭人陷害的牛仔，或因恶毒流言而受到怀疑的治安官；总之，是一个既与自己冲突、又与边疆环境冲突的人。

usage.note: 用于说明观点、形象等产生的根源；firmly 加强其稳固程度。
usage.example: He had lived in it as a child when it was already disappearing, and his hero was firmly rooted in his memories and experiences, and in both the history and the mythology of the vanished frontier.
usage.exampleZh: 他小时候曾住在那里，而那时旧西部就已经在消失；他塑造的英雄牢牢扎根于自己的记忆和经历，也扎根于那片已经消逝的边疆的历史和传说。

usage.note: 可指合作，此处比喻神话与现实在同一主题上重合。
usage.example: And although no period or place in American history has been more absurdly romanticized, myth and reality did join hands in at least one arena, the conflict between the individual and encroaching civilization.
usage.exampleZh: 美国历史上没有哪个时代、哪个地方曾被如此荒唐地浪漫化；然而，神话和现实至少在一个领域确实携起了手，那就是个人与不断推进的文明之间的冲突。

usage.note: by 在此表示遵循，a code to live by 即供人生遵守的准则。
usage.example: We still do; living in a world in which undeclared aggression, war, hypocrisy, chicanery, anarchy and impending immolation are part of our daily lives, we all want a code to live by.
usage.exampleZh: 我们现在仍然如此；在我们生活的世界里，不宣而行的侵略、战争、虚伪、欺诈、无政府状态和迫近的毁灭，已是日常生活的一部分，所以我们都想要一套可以遵循的行为准则。

rows.en: Why does the idea of progress loom so large in the modern world?
rows.zh: 为什么进步的观念在现代世界中占据如此突出的位置？
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Surely because progress of a particular kind is actually taking place around us and is becoming more and more manifest.
rows.zh: 无疑是因为，某一种进步确实正在我们周围发生，而且变得越来越明显。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Although mankind has undergone no general improvement in intelligence or morality, it has made extraordinary progress in the accumulation of knowledge.
rows.zh: 人类的智力或道德虽然没有普遍提高，但在知识积累方面却取得了非凡的进展。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Knowledge began to increase as soon as the thoughts of one individual could be communicated to another by means of speech.
rows.zh: 一旦个人的思想能够通过言语传递给他人，知识就开始增长了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: With the invention of writing, a great advance was made, for knowledge could then be not only communicated but also stored.
rows.zh: 文字的发明带来了重大的进步，因为此后知识不仅能传播，还能储存。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Libraries made education possible, and education in its turn added to libraries: the growth of knowledge followed a kind of compound interest law, which was greatly enhanced by the invention of printing.
rows.zh: 图书馆使教育成为可能，教育反过来又充实了图书馆：知识的增长遵循着某种复利规律，而印刷术的发明大大加强了这一过程。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: All this was comparatively slow until, with the coming of science, the tempo was suddenly raised.
rows.zh: 这一切原先都进展得比较缓慢，直到科学出现，步伐才突然加快。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Then knowledge began to be accumulated according to a systematic plan.
rows.zh: 此后，知识开始按系统的计划积累起来。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The trickle became a stream; the stream has now become a torrent.
rows.zh: 细流变成了溪流，而如今溪流又变成了洪流。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Moreover, as soon as new knowledge is acquired, it is now turned to practical account.
rows.zh: 而且，现在新知识一旦获得，便立刻被用于实际。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: What is called ‘modern civilization’ is not the result of a balanced development of all man’s nature, but of accumulated knowledge applied to practical life.
rows.zh: 所谓“现代文明”，并不是人性各方面均衡发展的结果，而是积累的知识被应用于实际生活的结果。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The problem now facing humanity is: What is going to be done with all this knowledge?
rows.zh: 人类如今面临的问题是：要拿这些知识做什么？
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: As is so often pointed out, knowledge is a two-edged weapon which can be used equally for good or evil.
rows.zh: 正如人们常常指出的，知识是一件双刃武器，既能用于行善，也能用于作恶。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It is now being used indifferently for both.
rows.zh: 如今，人们正不加区分地把它用于这两个方面。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Could any spectacle, for instance, be more grimly whimsical than that of gunners using science to shatter men’s bodies while, close at hand, surgeons use it to restore them?
rows.zh: 譬如，炮手利用科学把人的身体炸得血肉横飞，而就在附近，外科医生却用科学来修复这些身体；还有什么景象能比这更残酷而荒诞吗？
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: We have to ask ourselves very seriously what will happen if this twofold use of knowledge, with its ever-increasing power, continues.
rows.zh: 我们必须非常严肃地问自己：如果知识的力量不断增长，同时又继续被这样用于两个相反方面，将会发生什么？
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: 常用于问题或观念在思想、讨论中占很大分量的语境。
usage.example: Why does the idea of progress loom so large in the modern world?
usage.exampleZh: 为什么进步的观念在现代世界中占据如此突出的位置？

usage.meaning: 反过来；轮到其发挥作用时
usage.note: 强调前后事物相互促动，此处教育又促进馆藏增长。
usage.example: Libraries made education possible, and education in its turn added to libraries: the growth of knowledge followed a kind of compound interest law, which was greatly enhanced by the invention of printing.
usage.exampleZh: 图书馆使教育成为可能，教育反过来又充实了图书馆：知识的增长遵循着某种复利规律，而印刷术的发明大大加强了这一过程。

usage.note: turn something to account 表示把某物加以利用；practical 强调实际用途。
usage.example: Moreover, as soon as new knowledge is acquired, it is now turned to practical account.
usage.exampleZh: 而且，现在新知识一旦获得，便立刻被用于实际。

usage.note: 比喻既可能有益也可能有害的事物，不能只理解为带来好处。
usage.example: As is so often pointed out, knowledge is a two-edged weapon which can be used equally for good or evil.
usage.exampleZh: 正如人们常常指出的，知识是一件双刃武器，既能用于行善，也能用于作恶。

usage.note: at hand 可指空间上很近，也可指时间上即将到来；此处是地点。
usage.example: Could any spectacle, for instance, be more grimly whimsical than that of gunners using science to shatter men’s bodies while, close at hand, surgeons use it to restore them?
usage.exampleZh: 譬如，炮手利用科学把人的身体炸得血肉横飞，而就在附近，外科医生却用科学来修复这些身体；还有什么景象能比这更残酷而荒诞吗？

rows.en: No two sorts of birds practise quite the same sort of flight; the varieties are infinite; but two classes may be roughly seen.
rows.zh: 没有哪两类鸟的飞行方式完全相同，变化可谓无穷；不过大致可以分为两类。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Any ship that crosses the Pacific is accompanied for many days by the smaller albatross, which may keep company with the vessel for an hour without visible or more than occasional movement of wing.
rows.zh: 任何横渡太平洋的船，都会有体型较小的信天翁相伴多日；它可以跟着船飞一个小时，期间看不见它振翅，或至多偶尔振一下。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The currents of air that the walls of the ship direct upwards, as well as in the line of its course, are enough to give the great bird with its immense wings sufficient sustenance and progress.
rows.zh: 船体两侧使气流向上、同时沿着航向流动，这些气流就足以给这只双翼巨大的大鸟提供充分的升力和前进动力。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The albatross is the king of the gliders, the class of fliers which harness the air to their purpose, but must yield to its opposition.
rows.zh: 信天翁是滑翔鸟类之王；这一类飞行者利用空气来达到自己的目的，却必须在逆风面前让步。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In the contrary school, the duck is supreme.
rows.zh: 在相反的另一派中，鸭子最出色。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It comes nearer to the engines with which man has ‘conquered’ the air, as he boasts.
rows.zh: 它更接近人类自夸用来“征服”天空的那些发动机。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Duck, and like them the pigeons, are endowed with steel-like muscles, that are a good part of the weight of the bird, and these will ply the short wings with such irresistible power that they can bore for long distances through an opposing gale before exhaustion follows.
rows.zh: 鸭子和与之相似的鸽子，都有钢铁般的肌肉，肌肉占了体重的相当一部分；这些肌肉以不可阻挡的力量振动短翼，使它们能顶着强劲逆风钻行很远之后，才感到疲惫。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Their humbler followers, such as partridges, have a like power of strong propulsion, but soon tire.
rows.zh: 比它们稍逊一筹的同类，例如鹧鸪，也有类似的强劲推进力，不过很快就累了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: You may pick them up in utter exhaustion, if wind over the sea has driven them to a long journey.
rows.zh: 如果海上的风逼着它们长途飞行，你便可能在它们精疲力尽时将其捡起来。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The swallow shares the virtues of both schools in highest measure.
rows.zh: 燕子则把两派的优点发挥到了极致。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It tires not, nor does it boast of its power; but belongs to the air, travelling it may be six thousand miles to and from its northern nesting home, feeding its flown young as it flies, and slipping through a medium that seems to help its passage even when the wind is adverse.
rows.zh: 它不会疲倦，也不炫耀自己的力量；它属于天空，往返北方筑巢地的旅程可能长达六千英里，一边飞一边喂养已经离巢的幼鸟，轻捷地穿过空气；即使风向相反，这种介质似乎也在助它前行。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Such birds do us good, though we no longer take omens from their flight on this side and that; and even the most superstitious villagers no longer take off their hats to the magpie and wish it good-morning.
rows.zh: 这样的鸟使我们受益，尽管我们早已不再从它们忽而向这边、忽而向那边的飞行中占卜吉凶，就连最迷信的村民也不再向喜鹊脱帽，祝它早安了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: 此处指信天翁跟随船只飞行，不只限于人的交往。
usage.example: Any ship that crosses the Pacific is accompanied for many days by the smaller albatross, which may keep company with the vessel for an hour without visible or more than occasional movement of wing.
usage.exampleZh: 任何横渡太平洋的船，都会有体型较小的信天翁相伴多日；它可以跟着船飞一个小时，期间看不见它振翅，或至多偶尔振一下。

usage.note: 连接补充成分，此处是两种气流方向：向上与沿航线。
usage.example: The currents of air that the walls of the ship direct upwards, as well as in the line of its course, are enough to give the great bird with its immense wings sufficient sustenance and progress.
usage.exampleZh: 船体两侧使气流向上、同时沿着航向流动，这些气流就足以给这只双翼巨大的大鸟提供充分的升力和前进动力。

usage.note: to 后接阻力或对手，此处指逆向气流使滑翔受限。
usage.example: The albatross is the king of the gliders, the class of fliers which harness the air to their purpose, but must yield to its opposition.
usage.exampleZh: 信天翁是滑翔鸟类之王；这一类飞行者利用空气来达到自己的目的，却必须在逆风面前让步。

usage.note: 常用于天赋、能力或自然特征，语体较正式。
usage.example: Duck, and like them the pigeons, are endowed with steel-like muscles, that are a good part of the weight of the bird, and these will ply the short wings with such irresistible power that they can bore for long distances through an opposing gale before exhaustion follows.
usage.exampleZh: 鸭子和与之相似的鸽子，都有钢铁般的肌肉，肌肉占了体重的相当一部分；这些肌肉以不可阻挡的力量振动短翼，使它们能顶着强劲逆风钻行很远之后，才感到疲惫。

usage.note: utter 加强 exhaustion，强调体力完全耗尽。
usage.example: You may pick them up in utter exhaustion, if wind over the sea has driven them to a long journey.
usage.exampleZh: 如果海上的风逼着它们长途飞行，你便可能在它们精疲力尽时将其捡起来。

rows.en: A young man sees a sunset and, unable to understand or to express the emotion that it rouses in him, concludes that it must be the gateway to a world that lies beyond.
rows.zh: 一个青年看见落日，既无法理解也无法表达它在心中唤起的感情，便认定它必是通往彼岸世界的大门。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It is difficult for any of us in moments of intense aesthetic experience to resist the suggestion that we are catching a glimpse of a light that shines down to us from a different realm of existence, different and, because the experience is intensely moving, in some way higher.
rows.zh: 在强烈的审美体验中，我们任何人都很难不产生这样的感觉：自己正在瞥见一道从另一个存在境界照向我们的光；那个境界与此间不同，而且由于这种体验深深震撼人心，似乎在某种意义上也更高。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: And, though the gleams blind and dazzle, yet do they convey a hint of beauty and serenity greater than we have known or imagined.
rows.zh: 那些闪光虽使人目眩眼花，却仍向我们传递了一丝美与宁静，其程度超越了我们曾经认识或想象过的一切。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Greater too than we can describe; for language, which was invented to convey the meanings of this world, cannot readily be fitted to the uses of another.
rows.zh: 也超越了我们所能描述的程度；因为语言被创造出来，是为了传达这个世界的意义，无法轻易调整来满足另一个世界的用途。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: That all great art has this power of suggesting a world beyond is undeniable.
rows.zh: 一切伟大艺术都有这种使人联想到彼岸世界的力量，这是不可否认的。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In some moods, Nature shares it.
rows.zh: 在某些心境下，自然也拥有这种力量。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: There is no sky in June so blue that it does not point forward to a bluer, no sunset so beautiful that it does not waken the vision of a greater beauty, a vision which passes before it is fully glimpsed, and in passing leaves an indefinable longing and regret.
rows.zh: 六月的天空无论多么湛蓝，都指向一片更蓝的天空；落日无论多么美丽，都会唤起一种更伟大的美的幻象；那幻象尚未被看真切便已消逝，消逝时留下一种无法言明的向往与惋惜。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: But, if this world is not merely a bad joke, life a vulgar flare amid the cool radiance of the stars, and existence an empty laugh braying across the mysteries; if these intimations of a something behind and beyond are not evil humour born of indigestion, or whimsies sent by the devil to mock and madden us, if, in a word, beauty means something, yet we must not seek to interpret the meaning.
rows.zh: 但是，如果这个世界并非只是个恶劣的玩笑，生命并非群星清冷光辉中一团粗俗的火光，存在也并非穿越重重奥秘的一声空洞狂笑；如果这些关于背后和彼岸某种事物的暗示，不是消化不良引起的恶劣心绪，也不是魔鬼送来嘲弄我们、使我们发狂的怪念；总之，如果美确有意义，我们却仍不应企图解释这种意义。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: If we glimpse the unutterable, it is unwise to try to utter it, nor should we seek to invest with significance that which we cannot grasp.
rows.zh: 如果我们瞥见了不可言说之物，硬要说出它是不明智的；我们也不该试图赋予自己无法理解的东西某种意义。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Beauty in terms of our human meanings is meaningless.
rows.zh: 用人类的意义体系来衡量，美是没有意义的。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: gateway 既可指实体入口，也可比喻通往另一领域的途径。
usage.example: A young man sees a sunset and, unable to understand or to express the emotion that it rouses in him, concludes that it must be the gateway to a world that lies beyond.
usage.exampleZh: 一个青年看见落日，既无法理解也无法表达它在心中唤起的感情，便认定它必是通往彼岸世界的大门。

usage.note: 强调短暂而不完整的看见，glimpse 常用单数。
usage.example: It is difficult for any of us in moments of intense aesthetic experience to resist the suggestion that we are catching a glimpse of a light that shines down to us from a different realm of existence, different and, because the experience is intensely moving, in some way higher.
usage.exampleZh: 在强烈的审美体验中，我们任何人都很难不产生这样的感觉：自己正在瞥见一道从另一个存在境界照向我们的光；那个境界与此间不同，而且由于这种体验深深震撼人心，似乎在某种意义上也更高。

usage.note: 强调眼前之物使人联想到尚未出现或更进一步的事物，此处是更蓝的天空。
usage.example: There is no sky in June so blue that it does not point forward to a bluer, no sunset so beautiful that it does not waken the vision of a greater beauty, a vision which passes before it is fully glimpsed, and in passing leaves an indefinable longing and regret.
usage.exampleZh: 六月的天空无论多么湛蓝，都指向一片更蓝的天空；落日无论多么美丽，都会唤起一种更伟大的美的幻象；那幻象尚未被看真切便已消逝，消逝时留下一种无法言明的向往与惋惜。

usage.note: 用于概括前面的较长论述。
usage.example: But, if this world is not merely a bad joke, life a vulgar flare amid the cool radiance of the stars, and existence an empty laugh braying across the mysteries; if these intimations of a something behind and beyond are not evil humour born of indigestion, or whimsies sent by the devil to mock and madden us, if, in a word, beauty means something, yet we must not seek to interpret the meaning.
usage.exampleZh: 但是，如果这个世界并非只是个恶劣的玩笑，生命并非群星清冷光辉中一团粗俗的火光，存在也并非穿越重重奥秘的一声空洞狂笑；如果这些关于背后和彼岸某种事物的暗示，不是消化不良引起的恶劣心绪，也不是魔鬼送来嘲弄我们、使我们发狂的怪念；总之，如果美确有意义，我们却仍不应企图解释这种意义。

usage.note: invest something with significance/authority 是正式结构，不能译成资金投资。
usage.example: If we glimpse the unutterable, it is unwise to try to utter it, nor should we seek to invest with significance that which we cannot grasp.
usage.exampleZh: 如果我们瞥见了不可言说之物，硬要说出它是不明智的；我们也不该试图赋予自己无法理解的东西某种意义。

rows.en: Many people in industry and the Services, who have practical experience of noise, regard any investigation of this question as a waste of time; they are not prepared even to admit the possibility that noise affects people.
rows.zh: 工业界和军队中许多亲身接触过噪声的人，认为对这个问题作任何调查都是浪费时间；他们甚至不愿承认噪声有可能影响人。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: On the other hand, those who dislike noise will sometimes use most inadequate evidence to support their pleas for a quieter society.
rows.zh: 另一方面，厌恶噪声的人有时又会用极不充分的证据，来支持他们要求社会更安静的呼吁。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: This is a pity, because noise abatement really is a good cause, and it is likely to be discredited if it gets to be associated with bad science.
rows.zh: 这很可惜，因为减轻噪声确实是一项有益的事业；一旦与不严谨的科学牵扯在一起，它就很可能失去信誉。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: One allegation often made is that noise produces mental illness.
rows.zh: 人们经常提出的一种说法是：噪声会引起精神疾病。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: A recent article in a weekly newspaper, for instance, was headed with a striking illustration of a lady in a state of considerable distress, with the caption ‘She was yet another victim, reduced to a screaming wreck’.
rows.zh: 例如，最近一家周报的一篇文章，开头配了一幅引人注目的插图，画的是一位陷于极度痛苦的女士，图注写着：“她又成了一个受害者，精神垮掉，只会尖叫。”
rows.speaker: 旁白 / 报纸图注

rows.en: On turning eagerly to the text, one learns that the lady was a typist who found the sound of office typewriters worried her more and more until eventually she had to go into a mental hospital.
rows.zh: 急切地转看正文后才知道，这位女士是名打字员，办公室打字机的声音使她越来越不安，最后不得不住进精神病院。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Now the snag in this sort of anecdote is of course that one cannot distinguish cause and effect.
rows.zh: 当然，这类轶事的问题在于，我们分不清因果。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Was the noise a cause of the illness, or were the complaints about noise merely a symptom?
rows.zh: 究竟噪声是致病原因，还是抱怨噪声仅仅是一个症状？
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Another patient might equally well complain that her neighbours were combining to slander her and persecute her, and yet one might be cautious about believing this statement.
rows.zh: 另一名病人也完全可能抱怨邻居们合伙诽谤和迫害她，但对于这种说法，人们恐怕就会谨慎，不会轻信。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: What is needed in the case of noise is a study of large numbers of people living under noisy conditions, to discover whether they are mentally ill more often than other people are.
rows.zh: 对于噪声问题，所需要的是研究大量生活在嘈杂环境中的人，查明他们是否比其他人更经常患精神疾病。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Some time ago the United States Navy, for instance, examined a very large number of men working on aircraft carriers: the study was known as Project Anehin.
rows.zh: 例如，不久前美国海军对大量在航空母舰上工作的人员进行了检查，这项研究名叫“阿内欣计划”。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It can be unpleasant to live even several miles from an aerodrome; if you think what it must be like to share the deck of a ship with several squadrons of jet aircraft, you will realize that a modern navy is a good place to study noise.
rows.zh: 即使住在离机场几英里的地方，也可能令人不快；如果想想与好几个中队的喷气式飞机共处一艘军舰甲板会是什么滋味，你就会明白，现代海军是研究噪声的好地方。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: But neither psychiatric interviews nor objective tests were able to show any effects upon these American sailors.
rows.zh: 然而，无论精神科访谈还是客观测试，都没能显示出这些美国水兵受到任何影响。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: This result merely confirms earlier American and British studies: if there is any effect of noise upon mental health, it must be so small that present methods of psychiatric diagnosis cannot find it.
rows.zh: 这一结果不过是证实了美国和英国早先的研究：如果噪声对心理健康真有影响，那也一定小到现有精神科诊断方法无法发现的程度。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: That does not prove that it does not exist; but it does mean that noise is less dangerous than, say, being brought up in an orphanage — which really is a mental health hazard.
rows.zh: 这并不能证明这种影响不存在；但确实意味着，噪声的危险性低于例如在孤儿院长大——后者确实是心理健康的一项危险因素。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: 引入另一角度或相反倾向，常与前文形成对照。
usage.example: On the other hand, those who dislike noise will sometimes use most inadequate evidence to support their pleas for a quieter society.
usage.exampleZh: 另一方面，厌恶噪声的人有时又会用极不充分的证据，来支持他们要求社会更安静的呼吁。

usage.note: 后接 distress 等状态名词，常用于较正式的描述。
usage.example: A recent article in a weekly newspaper, for instance, was headed with a striking illustration of a lady in a state of considerable distress, with the caption ‘She was yet another victim, reduced to a screaming wreck’.
usage.exampleZh: 例如，最近一家周报的一篇文章，开头配了一幅引人注目的插图，画的是一位陷于极度痛苦的女士，图注写着：“她又成了一个受害者，精神垮掉，只会尖叫。”

usage.note: 用于说明另一种说法或情况同样说得通，不能理解为做得同样好。
usage.example: Another patient might equally well complain that her neighbours were combining to slander her and persecute her, and yet one might be cautious about believing this statement.
usage.exampleZh: 另一名病人也完全可能抱怨邻居们合伙诽谤和迫害她，但对于这种说法，人们恐怕就会谨慎，不会轻信。

usage.note: that 引出结果，small 表明影响微弱到无法检出的程度。
usage.example: This result merely confirms earlier American and British studies: if there is any effect of noise upon mental health, it must be so small that present methods of psychiatric diagnosis cannot find it.
usage.exampleZh: 这一结果不过是证实了美国和英国早先的研究：如果噪声对心理健康真有影响，那也一定小到现有精神科诊断方法无法发现的程度。

usage.note: 原文是被动动名词结构；地点状语说明成长环境。
usage.example: That does not prove that it does not exist; but it does mean that noise is less dangerous than, say, being brought up in an orphanage — which really is a mental health hazard.
usage.exampleZh: 这并不能证明这种影响不存在；但确实意味着，噪声的危险性低于例如在孤儿院长大——后者确实是心理健康的一项危险因素。

lessons.title: The past life of the earth

rows.en: It is animals and plants which lived in or near water whose remains are most likely to be preserved, for one of the necessary conditions of preservation is quick burial, and it is only in the seas and rivers, and sometimes lakes, where mud and silt have been continuously deposited, that bodies and the like can be rapidly covered over and preserved.
rows.zh: 最有可能保存下遗骸的，是生活在水中或水边的动植物，因为迅速掩埋是保存所必需的条件之一；只有在泥沙不断沉积的海洋、河流，以及有时的湖泊里，尸体之类的东西才能迅速被覆盖并保存下来。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: But even in the most favourable circumstances only a small fraction of the creatures that die are preserved in this way before decay sets in or, even more likely, before scavengers eat them.
rows.zh: 但即使条件最有利，在腐烂开始之前，或更可能在被食腐动物吃掉之前，死去的生物也只有一小部分能这样保存下来。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: After all, all living creatures live by feeding on something else, whether it be plant or animal, dead or alive, and it is only by chance that such a fate is avoided.
rows.zh: 毕竟，一切生物都靠吃别的东西为生，不管那是植物还是动物、死物还是活物；能逃过这种命运，只能靠偶然。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The remains of plants and animals that lived on land are much more rarely preserved, for there is seldom anything to cover them over.
rows.zh: 生活在陆地上的动植物遗骸更难保存，因为很少有东西将它们盖住。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: When you think of the innumerable birds that one sees flying about, not to mention the equally numerous small animals like field mice and voles which you do not see, it is very rarely that one comes across a dead body, except, of course, on the roads.
rows.zh: 想想我们看见的无数飞来飞去的鸟，还不必提那些同样众多、却看不见的田鼠、䶄鼠等小动物，我们却很少碰到尸体——当然，马路上的除外。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: They decompose and are quickly destroyed by the weather or eaten by some other creature.
rows.zh: 它们会腐烂，很快被风吹雨淋毁坏，或被别的生物吃掉。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It is almost always due to some very special circumstances that traces of land animals survive, as by falling into inaccessible caves, or into an ice crevasse, like the Siberian mammoths, when the whole animal is sometimes preserved, as in a refrigerator.
rows.zh: 陆地动物的遗迹能留存下来，几乎总是因为某些十分特殊的情形，例如掉进难以进入的洞穴，或像西伯利亚猛犸象那样落入冰缝；这时有时整个动物都能保存，仿佛放在冰箱里一样。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: This is what happened to the famous Beresovka mammoth which was found preserved and in good condition.
rows.zh: 著名的别列佐夫卡猛犸象就是如此，它被发现时保存得相当完好。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In his mouth were the remains of fir trees—the last meal that he had before he fell into the crevasse and broke his back.
rows.zh: 它嘴里还有冷杉的残屑——这是它跌入冰缝、摔断脊背之前的最后一餐。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The mammoth has now been restored in the Palaeontological Museum in St. Petersburg.
rows.zh: 如今，这头猛犸象已在圣彼得堡的古生物博物馆里复原陈列。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Other animals were trapped in tar pits, like the elephants, sabre-toothed cats, and numerous other creatures that are found at Rancho la Brea, which is now just a suburb of Los Angeles.
rows.zh: 还有些动物被困在沥青坑中，例如在拉布雷亚牧场发现的大象、剑齿猫和许多其他生物；那里如今只是洛杉矶的一个郊区。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Apparently what happened was that water collected on these tar pits, and the bigger animals like the elephants ventured out on to the apparently firm surface to drink, and were promptly bogged in the tar.
rows.zh: 事情显然是这样发生的：沥青坑上积了水，大象等大型动物冒险走上看似坚实的表面去喝水，立刻便陷进沥青里。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: And then, when they were dead, the carnivores, like the sabre-toothed cats and the giant wolves, came out to feed and suffered exactly the same fate.
rows.zh: 等它们死后，剑齿猫、巨狼等食肉动物出来取食，也遭遇了完全相同的命运。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: There are also endless numbers of birds in the tar as well.
rows.zh: 沥青里还有数不清的鸟。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: 常用于腐败、恶劣天气等不利状况的开始。
usage.example: But even in the most favourable circumstances only a small fraction of the creatures that die are preserved in this way before decay sets in or, even more likely, before scavengers eat them.
usage.exampleZh: 但即使条件最有利，在腐烂开始之前，或更可能在被食腐动物吃掉之前，死去的生物也只有一小部分能这样保存下来。

usage.note: 表示并非出于计划或必然。
usage.example: After all, all living creatures live by feeding on something else, whether it be plant or animal, dead or alive, and it is only by chance that such a fate is avoided.
usage.exampleZh: 毕竟，一切生物都靠吃别的东西为生，不管那是植物还是动物、死物还是活物；能逃过这种命运，只能靠偶然。

usage.note: 引入进一步补充或更有分量的事例。
usage.example: When you think of the innumerable birds that one sees flying about, not to mention the equally numerous small animals like field mice and voles which you do not see, it is very rarely that one comes across a dead body, except, of course, on the roads.
usage.exampleZh: 想想我们看见的无数飞来飞去的鸟，还不必提那些同样众多、却看不见的田鼠、䶄鼠等小动物，我们却很少碰到尸体——当然，马路上的除外。

usage.note: 强调无意中遇到，不是有目标地查找。
usage.example: When you think of the innumerable birds that one sees flying about, not to mention the equally numerous small animals like field mice and voles which you do not see, it is very rarely that one comes across a dead body, except, of course, on the roads.
usage.exampleZh: 想想我们看见的无数飞来飞去的鸟，还不必提那些同样众多、却看不见的田鼠、䶄鼠等小动物，我们却很少碰到尸体——当然，马路上的除外。

usage.note: suffer 与不幸的结果搭配；exactly 强调结局完全一样。
usage.example: And then, when they were dead, the carnivores, like the sabre-toothed cats and the giant wolves, came out to feed and suffered exactly the same fate.
usage.exampleZh: 等它们死后，剑齿猫、巨狼等食肉动物出来取食，也遭遇了完全相同的命运。

rows.en: From the seventeenth-century empire of Sweden, the story of a galleon that sank at the start of her maiden voyage in 1628 must be one of the strangest tales of the sea.
rows.zh: 在十七世纪瑞典帝国的历史中，一艘大型帆船于一六二八年首航刚开始便沉没的故事，一定算得上海上最离奇的传说之一。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: For nearly three and a half centuries she lay at the bottom of Stockholm harbour until her discovery in 1956.
rows.zh: 它在斯德哥尔摩港底躺了将近三个半世纪，直到一九五六年被发现。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: This was the Vasa, royal flagship of the great imperial fleet.
rows.zh: 这就是“瓦萨号”，庞大的帝国舰队的皇家旗舰。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: King Gustavus Adolphus, ‘The Northern Hurricane’, then at the height of his military success in the Thirty Years’ War, had dictated her measurements and armament.
rows.zh: 国王古斯塔夫·阿道夫号称“北方飓风”，当时在三十年战争中的军事成就正值顶峰；船的尺寸和武器配备都是由他亲自规定的。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Triple gun-decks mounted sixty-four bronze cannon.
rows.zh: 三层火炮甲板装有六十四门青铜炮。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: She was intended to play a leading role in the growing might of Sweden.
rows.zh: 这艘船原本要在瑞典不断增强的国力中扮演主角。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: As she was prepared for her maiden voyage on August 10, 1628, Stockholm was in a ferment.
rows.zh: 一六二八年八月十日，当它准备首航时，整个斯德哥尔摩都沸腾了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: From the Skeppsbron and surrounding islands the people watched this thing of beauty begin to spread her sails and catch the wind.
rows.zh: 人们从斯凯普斯布隆码头和周围岛屿上，望着这件美丽的造物开始扬帆迎风。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: They had laboured for three years to produce this floating work of art; she was more richly carved and ornamented than any previous ship.
rows.zh: 他们辛劳了三年才造出这件浮动的艺术品；它的雕刻和装饰之华丽，胜过此前任何一艘船。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The high stern castle was a riot of carved gods, demons, knights, kings, warriors, mermaids, cherubs; and zoomorphic animal shapes ablaze with red and gold and blue, symbols of courage, power, and cruelty, were portrayed to stir the imaginations of the superstitious sailors of the day.
rows.zh: 高高的艉楼上，各种神祇、恶魔、骑士、国王、武士、美人鱼和小天使雕像纷繁夺目；还有红、金、蓝色灿烂耀眼的兽形图像，象征勇气、力量和残酷，用来激起那个时代迷信水手的想象。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Then the cannons of the anchored warships thundered a salute to which the Vasa fired in reply.
rows.zh: 接着，停泊的军舰鸣炮致敬，“瓦萨号”也鸣炮回礼。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: As she emerged from her drifting cloud of gun smoke with the water churned to foam beneath her bow, her flags flying, pennants waving, sails filling in the breeze, and the red and gold of her superstructure ablaze with colour, she presented a more majestic spectacle than Stockholmers had ever seen before.
rows.zh: 它从自己漂浮的炮烟中驶出，船首下海水翻成白沫，旗帜飞扬，长旗飘动，船帆被微风鼓满，上层建筑红金交映，色彩灿烂；它展现的雄伟景象，是斯德哥尔摩人此前从未见过的。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: All gun-ports were open and the muzzles peeped wickedly from them.
rows.zh: 所有炮门都敞着，炮口从中探出，显得凶险逼人。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: As the wind freshened there came a sudden squall and the ship made a strange movement, listing to port.
rows.zh: 风渐渐加大，突然一阵狂风袭来，船出现了奇怪的晃动，向左舷倾斜。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The Ordnance Officer ordered all the port cannon to be heaved to starboard to counteract the list, but the steepening angle of the decks increased.
rows.zh: 军械官命令把左舷全部大炮拖到右舷，以抵消船身倾斜，但甲板的倾角却继续增大。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Then the sound of rumbling thunder reached the watchers on the shore, as cargo, ballast, ammunition and 400 people went sliding and crashing down to the port side of the steeply listing ship.
rows.zh: 随后，岸上观众听到雷鸣般的轰隆声，货物、压舱物、弹药和四百个人一起滑落，猛撞向这艘严重倾斜的船的左舷。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The lower gun-ports were now below water and the inrush sealed the ship’s fate.
rows.zh: 下层炮门此时已没入水下，涌入的海水决定了这艘船的厄运。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In that first glorious hour, the mighty Vasa, which was intended to rule the Baltic, sank with all flags flying—in the harbour of her birth.
rows.zh: 就在最初那辉煌的一小时里，本打算称霸波罗的海的强大“瓦萨号”，旗帜依旧飘扬，却沉没在了它诞生的港湾。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: 专指船只第一次正式航行，maiden 在此意为首次的。
usage.example: From the seventeenth-century empire of Sweden, the story of a galleon that sank at the start of her maiden voyage in 1628 must be one of the strangest tales of the sea.
usage.exampleZh: 在十七世纪瑞典帝国的历史中，一艘大型帆船于一六二八年首航刚开始便沉没的故事，一定算得上海上最离奇的传说之一。

usage.note: 描述事业、力量、活动等最盛的时期。
usage.example: King Gustavus Adolphus, ‘The Northern Hurricane’, then at the height of his military success in the Thirty Years’ War, had dictated her measurements and armament.
usage.exampleZh: 国王古斯塔夫·阿道夫号称“北方飓风”，当时在三十年战争中的军事成就正值顶峰；船的尺寸和武器配备都是由他亲自规定的。

usage.note: 常接 in，leading 表示主要或领头的地位。
usage.example: She was intended to play a leading role in the growing might of Sweden.
usage.exampleZh: 这艘船原本要在瑞典不断增强的国力中扮演主角。

usage.note: ferment 这里比喻群体情绪沸腾，而非实际发酵。
usage.example: As she was prepared for her maiden voyage on August 10, 1628, Stockholm was in a ferment.
usage.exampleZh: 一六二八年八月十日，当它准备首航时，整个斯德哥尔摩都沸腾了。

usage.note: 通常指使坏结局不可避免；所有格可换成具体对象。
usage.example: The lower gun-ports were now below water and the inrush sealed the ship’s fate.
usage.exampleZh: 下层炮门此时已没入水下，涌入的海水决定了这艘船的厄运。

rows.en: This is a sceptical age, but although our faith in many of the things in which our forefathers fervently believed has weakened, our confidence in the curative properties of the bottle of medicine remains the same as theirs.
rows.zh: 这是一个怀疑的时代；虽然我们对祖先曾热烈信奉的许多事物已减弱了信仰，但对那一瓶药的疗效，我们仍然和他们一样充满信心。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: This modern faith in medicines is proved by the fact that the annual drug bill of the Health Services is mounting to astronomical figures and shows no signs at present of ceasing to rise.
rows.zh: 卫生服务部门每年的药费已攀升到天文数字，而且目前毫无停止上涨的迹象，这一事实证明了现代人对药物的这种信仰。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The majority of the patients attending the medical out-patients departments of our hospitals feel that they have not received adequate treatment unless they are able to carry home with them some tangible remedy in the shape of a bottle of medicine, a box of pills, or a small jar of ointment, and the doctor in charge of the department is only too ready to provide them with these requirements.
rows.zh: 到我们医院内科门诊就诊的多数病人，除非能带回家一些看得见摸得着的药物，比如一瓶药水、一盒药片或一小罐药膏，否则便觉得自己没有受到充分治疗；而科室负责的医生也极愿意满足这些要求。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: There is no quicker method of disposing of patients than by giving them what they are asking for, and since most medical men in the Health Services are overworked and have little time for offering time-consuming and little-appreciated advice on such subjects as diet, right living, and the need for abandoning bad habits etc., the bottle, the box, and the jar are almost always granted them.
rows.zh: 要尽快打发病人，没有什么办法比给他们想要的东西更快；卫生服务部门的大多数医生又都工作过量，几乎没时间提供那些费时却不太受重视的忠告，例如饮食、正确的生活方式、戒除坏习惯的必要性等等，因此病人几乎总能拿到那瓶药、那盒药片和那罐药膏。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Nor is it only the ignorant and ill-educated person who has such faith in the bottle of medicine.
rows.zh: 对药瓶抱有这种信念的，也并非只有无知和受教育少的人。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It is recounted of Thomas Carlyle that when he heard of the illness of his friend, Henry Taylor, he went off immediately to visit him, carrying with him in his pocket what remained of a bottle of medicine formerly prescribed for an indisposition of Mrs. Carlyle’s.
rows.zh: 据说托马斯·卡莱尔听到朋友亨利·泰勒生病后，立刻动身去看他，口袋里带着一瓶剩药；那原是医生早先为卡莱尔夫人的一次小病开的。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Carlyle was entirely ignorant of what the bottle in his pocket contained, of the nature of the illness from which his friend was suffering, and of what had previously been wrong with his wife, but a medicine that had worked so well in one form of illness would surely be of equal benefit in another, and comforted by the thought of the help he was bringing to his friend, he hastened to Henry Taylor's house.
rows.zh: 卡莱尔全然不知道口袋里的瓶子装着什么药，不知道朋友患的是什么病，也不知道妻子先前哪里不舒服；但他觉得，既然一种药对某种病如此有效，对另一种病肯定同样有益，于是想到自己正给朋友送去帮助，心中甚感宽慰，便急忙赶往亨利·泰勒家。
rows.speaker: 旁白 / 卡莱尔的想法

rows.en: History does not relate whether his friend accepted his medical help, but in all probability he did.
rows.zh: 历史没有记载他的朋友是否接受了这番医药帮助，但他十之八九接受了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The great advantage of taking medicine is that it makes no demands on the taker beyond that of putting up for a moment with a disgusting taste, and that is what all patients demand of their doctors—to be cured at no inconvenience to themselves.
rows.zh: 吃药最大的好处是，除了短暂忍受一点恶心的味道，对吃药者没有别的要求；而这正是所有病人向医生提出的要求——自己不受任何麻烦，病就能治好。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Many strange new means of transport have been developed in our century, the strangest of them being perhaps the hovercraft.
rows.zh: 本世纪已开发出许多奇特的新交通工具，其中最奇特的也许是气垫船。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In 1953, a former electronics engineer in his fifties, Christopher Cockerell, who had turned to boat-building on the Norfolk Broads, suggested an idea on which he had been working for many years to the British Government and industrial circles.
rows.zh: 一九五三年，五十多岁的克里斯托弗·科克雷尔原是一名电子工程师，后来在诺福克湖区转行造船；他向英国政府和工业界提出了一个自己钻研多年的构想。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It was the idea of supporting a craft on a ‘pad’, or cushion, of low-pressure air, ringed with a curtain of higher pressure air.
rows.zh: 这个构想是让船体由一层低压空气“垫子”，也就是气垫支撑起来，四周再围以较高压力的空气帘。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Ever since, people have had difficulty in deciding whether the craft should be ranged among ships, planes, or land vehicles—for it is something in between a boat and an aircraft.
rows.zh: 自那以后，人们一直难以确定，这种交通工具应归入船舶、飞机，还是陆上车辆，因为它是介于船与飞机之间的东西。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: As a shipbuilder, Cockerell was trying to find a solution to the problem of the wave resistance which wastes a good deal of a surface ship’s power and limits its speed.
rows.zh: 作为造船者，科克雷尔一直试图解决兴波阻力的问题；这种阻力耗费水面船舶的大量动力，并限制船速。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: His answer was to lift the vessel out of the water by making it ride on a cushion of air, no more than one or two feet thick.
rows.zh: 他的办法是让船乘在一层仅一两英尺厚的气垫上，从而离开水面。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: This is done by a great number of ring-shaped air jets on the bottom of the craft.
rows.zh: 船底大量环形空气喷口实现了这一点。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It ‘flies’, therefore, but it cannot fly higher—its action depends on the surface, water or ground, over which it rides.
rows.zh: 因此它是在“飞行”，却又飞不高，因为它的运行依赖于所乘行的水面或地面。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The first tests on the Solent in 1959 caused a sensation.
rows.zh: 一九五九年在索伦特海峡进行的首次试验轰动一时。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The hovercraft travelled first over the water, then mounted the beach, climbed up the dunes, and sat down on a road.
rows.zh: 气垫船先驶过水面，然后登上海滩，爬上沙丘，落到一条公路上。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Later it crossed the Channel, riding smoothly over the waves, which presented no problem.
rows.zh: 后来它又横渡了英吉利海峡，平稳地越过波浪，海浪没有造成任何问题。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Since that time, various types of hovercraft have appeared and taken up regular service.
rows.zh: 从那以后，各种型号的气垫船陆续出现，并开始定期运营。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The hovercraft is particularly useful in large areas with poor communications such as Africa or Australia; it can become a ‘flying fruit-bowl’, carrying bananas from the plantations to the ports; giant hovercraft liners could span the Atlantic; and the railway of the future may well be the ‘hovertrain’, riding on its air cushion over a single rail, which it never touches, at speeds up to 300 m.p.h.—the possibilities appear unlimited.
rows.zh: 气垫船特别适用于非洲或澳大利亚这类交通不便的广大地区；它可以成为“飞行的果盘”，把香蕉从种植园运到港口；巨型气垫客轮可以横跨大西洋；未来的铁路很可能采用“气垫列车”，让它乘着气垫在从不接触的单轨上方运行，时速可达三百英里——种种可能性似乎没有尽头。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Our knowledge of the oceans a hundred years ago was confined to the two-dimensional shape of the sea surface and the hazards of navigation presented by the irregularities in depth of the shallow water close to the land.
rows.zh: 一百年前，我们对海洋的认识，仅限于海面的二维形状，以及近岸浅水区深浅不一给航行带来的危险。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The open sea was deep and mysterious, and anyone who gave more than a passing thought to the bottom confines of the oceans probably assumed that the sea bed was flat.
rows.zh: 外海深邃而神秘；凡对海洋底部不止略微想过一下的人，多半都以为海床是平的。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Sir James Clark Ross had obtained a sounding of over 2,400 fathoms in 1839, but it was not until 1869, when H. M. S. Porcupine was put at the disposal of the Royal Society for several cruises, that a series of deep soundings was obtained in the Atlantic and the first samples were collected by dredging the bottom.
rows.zh: 詹姆斯·克拉克·罗斯爵士在一八三九年已测得超过二千四百英寻的深度，但直到一八六九年，英国皇家海军“豪猪号”被交给皇家学会使用、进行了数次考察航行之后，人们才取得大西洋的一系列深海测深数据，并通过在海底拖捞采到了第一批样本。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Shortly after this the famous H. M. S. Challenger expedition established the study of the sea-floor as a subject worthy of the most qualified physicists and geologists.
rows.zh: 此后不久，著名的皇家海军“挑战者号”考察，使海底研究确立为一个值得最优秀的物理学家和地质学家投入的课题。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: A burst of activity associated with the laying of submarine cables soon confirmed the Challenger’s observation that many parts of the ocean were two to three miles deep, and the existence of underwater features of considerable magnitude.
rows.zh: 铺设海底电缆带来的一阵活跃工作，很快证实了“挑战者号”的观测：海洋许多地方深达两三英里，而且存在规模相当可观的水下地形。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Today, enough soundings are available to enable a relief map of the Atlantic to be drawn and we know something of the great variety of the sea bed’s topography.
rows.zh: 如今已有足够的测深数据，可以绘出大西洋的地形起伏图，我们也对海床地形的丰富多样有所了解。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Since the sea covers the greater part of the earth’s surface, it is quite reasonable to regard the sea floor as the basic form of the crust of the earth, with, superimposed upon it the continents, together with the islands and other features of the oceans.
rows.zh: 海洋覆盖着地球表面的大部分，因此把海底看作地壳的基本形态，是很合理的；大陆以及海洋中的岛屿和其他地形，都叠置在这个基本形态之上。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The continents form rugged tablelands which stand nearly three miles above the floor of the open ocean.
rows.zh: 大陆形成崎岖的高台地，耸立在外海海底之上，高出将近三英里。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: From the shore line, out to a distance which may be anywhere from a few miles to a few hundred miles, runs the gentle slope of the continental shelf, geologically part of the continents.
rows.zh: 从海岸线向外延伸几英里到几百英里不等，是大陆架的缓坡；从地质上说，它属于大陆的一部分。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The real dividing line between continents and oceans occurs at the foot of a steeper slope.
rows.zh: 大陆与海洋真正的分界线，位于一段更陡的坡的坡脚。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: This continental slope usually starts at a place somewhere near the 100-fathom mark and in the course of a few hundred miles reaches the true ocean floor at 2,500-3,500 fathoms.
rows.zh: 这种大陆坡通常从约一百英寻深处开始，延伸几百英里后，到达深二千五百至三千五百英寻的真正洋底。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The slope averages about 1 in 30, but contains steep, probably vertical, cliffs, and gentle sediment-covered terraces, and near its lower reaches there is a long tailing-off which is almost certainly the result of material transported out to deep water after being eroded from the continental masses.
rows.zh: 其坡度平均约为三十分之一，但其中有陡峭、很可能垂直的断崖，也有覆盖沉积物的平缓台阶；在较低地段附近，坡势又有很长一段逐渐变缓，这几乎肯定是大陆块体遭侵蚀后，物质被搬运到深水处所造成的。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.exampleZh: 詹姆斯·克拉克·罗斯爵士在一八三九年已测得超过二千四百英寻的深度，但直到一八六九年，英国皇家海军“豪猪号”被交给皇家学会使用、进行了数次考察航行之后，人们才取得大西洋的一系列深海测深数据，并通过在海底拖捞采到了第一批样本。

usage.note: of 后接名词；此处表示值得最优秀学者研究。
usage.example: Shortly after this the famous H. M. S. Challenger expedition established the study of the sea-floor as a subject worthy of the most qualified physicists and geologists.
usage.exampleZh: 此后不久，著名的皇家海军“挑战者号”考察，使海底研究确立为一个值得最优秀的物理学家和地质学家投入的课题。

usage.note: 通常指时间过程，原文用于延伸几百英里的空间过程。
usage.example: This continental slope usually starts at a place somewhere near the 100-fathom mark and in the course of a few hundred miles reaches the true ocean floor at 2,500-3,500 fathoms.
usage.exampleZh: 这种大陆坡通常从约一百英寻深处开始，延伸几百英里后，到达深二千五百至三千五百英寻的真正洋底。

rows.en: Appreciation of sculpture depends upon the ability to respond to form in three dimensions.
rows.zh: 欣赏雕塑，有赖于对三维形体作出感受和反应的能力。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: That is perhaps why sculpture has been described as the most difficult of all arts; certainly it is more difficult than the arts which involve appreciation of flat forms, shape in only two dimensions.
rows.zh: 这也许就是雕塑被称为所有艺术中最难的一门的原因；可以肯定，它比那些欣赏平面形态、只涉及二维形状的艺术更难。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Many more people are ‘form-blind’ than colour-blind.
rows.zh: “形盲”的人远比色盲的人多。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The child learning to see, first distinguishes only two-dimensional shape; it cannot judge distances, depths.
rows.zh: 儿童学习看东西时，最初只能分辨二维形状，还不能判断远近和深浅。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Later, for its personal safety and practical needs, it has to develop (partly by means of touch) the ability to judge roughly three-dimensional distances.
rows.zh: 后来，为了自身安全和实际需要，他必须发展出粗略判断三维距离的能力，其中一部分要借助触摸。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: But having satisfied the requirements of practical necessity, most people go no further.
rows.zh: 然而，大多数人在满足实际需要之后，就不再向前发展了。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Though they may attain considerable accuracy in the perception of flat form, they do not make the further intellectual and emotional effort needed to comprehend form in its full spatial existence.
rows.zh: 他们对平面形态的感知也许相当准确，却不再付出进一步的智力与情感努力，去理解形体完整的空间存在。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: This is what the sculptor must do.
rows.zh: 而雕塑家必须做到这一点。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He must strive continually to think of, and use, form in its full spatial completeness.
rows.zh: 他必须不断努力，从形体完整的空间形态出发来思考和运用它。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He gets the solid shape, as it were, inside his head—he thinks of it, whatever its size, as if he were holding it completely enclosed in the hollow of his hand.
rows.zh: 可以说，他把实体形状放进了脑子里；不论它有多大，他在思考它时，都仿佛将它完整地握在自己的掌心中。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He mentally visualizes a complex form from all round itself; he knows while he looks at one side what the other side is like; he identifies himself with its centre of gravity, its mass, its weight; he realizes its volume, as the space that the shape displaces in the air.
rows.zh: 他在心中从四面八方呈现一个复杂形体；看着一面时，就知道另一面是什么样；他把自己融入它的重心、体量和重量之中，把它的体积理解为这个形状在空气中所占据的空间。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: And the sensitive observer of sculpture must also learn to feel shape simply as shape, not as description or reminiscence.
rows.zh: 同样，对雕塑敏感的观赏者也必须学会，只把形状当作形状来感受，不把它当作某种描摹或记忆的唤起。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He must, for example, perceive an egg as a simple single solid shape, quite apart from its significance as food, or from the literary idea that it will become a bird.
rows.zh: 例如，他必须把鸡蛋看成一个简单、单一的实体形状，完全撇开它作为食物的意义，也撇开“它将变成一只鸟”这种文学性的联想。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: And so with solids such as a shell, a nut, a plum, a pear, a tadpole, a mushroom, a mountain peak, a kidney, a carrot, a tree-trunk, a bird, a bud, a lark, a ladybird, a bulrush, a bone.
rows.zh: 对其他实体也应如此，例如贝壳、坚果、李子、梨、蝌蚪、蘑菇、山峰、肾脏、胡萝卜、树干、鸟、花蕾、云雀、瓢虫、芦苇和骨头。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: From these he can go on to appreciate more complex forms or combinations of several forms.
rows.zh: 由此，他就能进而欣赏更复杂的形体，或几个形体的组合。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: dimension 指空间维度；three dimensions 涉及长、宽、高。
usage.example: Appreciation of sculpture depends upon the ability to respond to form in three dimensions.
usage.exampleZh: 欣赏雕塑，有赖于对三维形体作出感受和反应的能力。

usage.note: 表示发展或行动就此停止，further 在此是副词。
usage.example: But having satisfied the requirements of practical necessity, most people go no further.
usage.exampleZh: 然而，大多数人在满足实际需要之后，就不再向前发展了。

usage.note: 插入语，提示表达是比喻或并不完全按字面理解。
usage.example: He gets the solid shape, as it were, inside his head—he thinks of it, whatever its size, as if he were holding it completely enclosed in the hollow of his hand.
usage.exampleZh: 可以说，他把实体形状放进了脑子里；不论它有多大，他在思考它时，都仿佛将它完整地握在自己的掌心中。

usage.note: apart from 此处不是此外还有，而是排除其他意义，只看形体。
usage.example: He must, for example, perceive an egg as a simple single solid shape, quite apart from its significance as food, or from the literary idea that it will become a bird.
usage.exampleZh: 例如，他必须把鸡蛋看成一个简单、单一的实体形状，完全撇开它作为食物的意义，也撇开“它将变成一只鸟”这种文学性的联想。

usage.note: 后接动词原形，表示完成前一步后转入下一步。
usage.example: From these he can go on to appreciate more complex forms or combinations of several forms.
usage.exampleZh: 由此，他就能进而欣赏更复杂的形体，或几个形体的组合。

rows.en: In his own lifetime Galileo was the centre of violent controversy; but the scientific dust has long since settled, and today we can see even his famous clash with the Inquisition in something like its proper perspective.
rows.zh: 伽利略在世时曾是激烈争论的中心；但科学争论的尘埃早已落定，如今即使是他与宗教裁判所那场著名的冲突，我们也能够以近乎恰当的视角来看待。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: But, in contrast, it is only in modern times that Galileo has become a problem child for historians of science.
rows.zh: 可形成对照的是，直到近代，伽利略才成了让科学史家头疼的“问题孩子”。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: The old view of Galileo was delightfully uncomplicated.
rows.zh: 过去对伽利略的看法，简单得令人愉快。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He was, above all, a man who experimented: who despised the prejudices and book learning of the Aristotelians, who put his questions to nature instead of to the ancients, and who drew his conclusions fearlessly.
rows.zh: 他首先是一个实验者：鄙视亚里士多德学派的偏见和书本知识，向自然发问而不向古人讨教，并且无所畏惧地得出自己的结论。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He had been the first to turn a telescope to the sky, and he had seen there evidence enough to overthrow Aristotle and Ptolemy together.
rows.zh: 他第一个把望远镜指向天空，并在那里看到了足以把亚里士多德和托勒密一并推翻的证据。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: He was the man who climbed the Leaning Tower of Pisa and dropped various weights from the top, who rolled balls down inclined planes, and then generalized the results of his many experiments into the famous law of free fall.
rows.zh: 他就是那个登上比萨斜塔、从塔顶放下各种重物的人，也是那个让球沿斜面滚下，然后把许多实验的结果概括成著名的自由落体定律的人。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: But a closer study of the evidence, supported by a deeper sense of the period, and particularly by a new consciousness of the philosophical undercurrents in the scientific revolution, has profoundly modified this view of Galileo.
rows.zh: 然而，对证据作更仔细的研究，加上对那个时代更深的理解，特别是重新意识到科学革命背后的哲学暗流，已经深刻地改变了这种伽利略观。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Today, although the old Galileo lives on in many popular writings, among historians of science a new and more sophisticated picture has emerged.
rows.zh: 如今，旧的伽利略形象虽仍活在许多通俗著作中，但在科学史家中，一个崭新而更复杂精细的形象已经出现。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: At the same time our sympathy for Galileo's opponents has grown somewhat.
rows.zh: 与此同时，我们对伽利略的反对者也多了几分同情。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: His telescopic observations are justly immortal; they aroused great interest at the time, they had important theoretical consequences, and they provided a striking demonstration of the potentialities hidden in instruments and apparatus.
rows.zh: 他的望远镜观测理当不朽；这些观测在当时引起了极大兴趣，产生了重要的理论影响，也鲜明地展示了仪器和设备中潜藏的种种可能。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: But can we blame those who looked and failed to see what Galileo saw, if we remember that to use a telescope at the limit of its powers calls for long experience and intimate familiarity with one’s instrument?
rows.zh: 不过，如果想到把望远镜的性能发挥到极限，需要长期经验和对仪器的深入熟悉，我们还能责怪那些看了却看不出伽利略所见之物的人吗？
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Was the philosopher who refused to look through Galileo's telescope more culpable than those who alleged that the spiral nebulae observed with Lord Rosse’s great telescope in the eighteen-forties were scratches left by the grinder?
rows.zh: 那个拒绝透过伽利略望远镜观看的哲学家，难道比另一些人更应受责备吗？后者曾宣称，十九世纪四十年代用罗斯勋爵的大望远镜观测到的旋涡星云，不过是磨镜人留下的划痕。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: We can perhaps forgive those who said the moons of Jupiter were produced by Galileo's spyglass if we recall that in his day, as for centuries before, curved glass was the popular contrivance for producing not truth but illusion, untruth; and if a single curved glass would distort nature, how much more would a pair of them?
rows.zh: 如果我们想起，在伽利略的时代以及此前几个世纪，曲面玻璃一向是用来制造幻象和假象、而非揭示真相的常见工具，我们也许就能原谅那些说木星卫星是伽利略的望远镜制造出来的人；既然一片曲面玻璃就会使自然景物变形，两片岂不会更严重？
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: 通常与完成时或过去时连用，强调很久以前就已发生。
usage.example: In his own lifetime Galileo was the centre of violent controversy; but the scientific dust has long since settled, and today we can see even his famous clash with the Inquisition in something like its proper perspective.
usage.exampleZh: 伽利略在世时曾是激烈争论的中心；但科学争论的尘埃早已落定，如今即使是他与宗教裁判所那场著名的冲突，我们也能够以近乎恰当的视角来看待。

rows.en: Education is one of the key words of our time.
rows.zh: 教育是我们时代的关键词之一。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: A man without an education, many of us believe, is an unfortunate victim of adverse circumstances, deprived of one of the greatest twentieth-century opportunities.
rows.zh: 我们许多人认为，一个没有受过教育的人，是恶劣环境的不幸牺牲者，被剥夺了二十世纪最重要的机会之一。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Convinced of the importance of education, modern states ‘invest’ in institutions of learning to get back ‘interest’ in the form of a large group of enlightened young men and women who are potential leaders.
rows.zh: 现代国家确信教育的重要性，于是向教育机构“投资”，以一大批思想开明、具有领导潜能的青年男女作为收回的“利息”。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Education, with its cycles of instruction so carefully worked out, punctuated by textbooks—those purchasable wells of wisdom—what would civilization be like without its benefits?
rows.zh: 教育有着精心安排的教学阶段，阶段之间又配置着教科书——那些花钱就能买到的智慧之泉；倘若没有教育的种种益处，文明会是什么样子呢？
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: So much is certain: that we would have doctors and preachers, lawyers and defendants, marriages and births—but our spiritual outlook would be different.
rows.zh: 有一点是肯定的：我们仍会有医生和传教士、律师和被告，仍会有婚嫁和生育，但我们的精神面貌会不同。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: We would lay less stress on ‘facts and figures’ and more on a good memory, on applied psychology, and on the capacity of a man to get along with his fellow-citizens.
rows.zh: 我们会较少重视“事实和数字”，而更重视良好的记忆力、实用心理知识，以及人与其他公民和睦相处的能力。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: If our educational system were fashioned after its bookless past we would have the most democratic form of ‘college’ imaginable.
rows.zh: 假如我们的教育制度仿照从前没有书本的模式来构建，我们就会拥有想象得到的最民主的“学院”。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Among tribal people all knowledge inherited by tradition is shared by all; it is taught to every member of the tribe so that in this respect everybody is equally equipped for life.
rows.zh: 在部落民族中，所有依靠传统继承下来的知识都是人人共享的；每个部落成员都会接受这些知识的传授，所以在这一点上，每个人都同样做好了生活的准备。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: It is the ideal condition of the ‘equal start’ which only our most progressive forms of modern education try to regain.
rows.zh: 这正是“起点平等”的理想状态，而现代教育中只有最进步的形式，才试图重新获得它。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: In primitive cultures the obligation to seek and to receive the traditional instruction is binding to all.
rows.zh: 在原始文化中，寻求和接受传统教育是对所有人都有约束力的义务。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: There are no ‘illiterates’—if the term can be applied to peoples without a script—while our own compulsory school attendance became law in Germany in 1642, in France in 1806, and in England in 1876, and is still non-existent in a number of ‘civilized’ nations.
rows.zh: 那里没有“文盲”——假如这个词可以用来称呼没有文字的民族中的人——而我们自己的强制入学制度，直到德国的一六四二年、法国的一八〇六年、英国的一八七六年才成为法律，在许多“文明”国家甚至至今仍不存在。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: This shows how long it was before we deemed it necessary to make sure that all our children could share in the knowledge accumulated by the ‘happy few’ during the past centuries.
rows.zh: 这表明，过了何等漫长的岁月，我们才认为有必要确保所有孩子都能分享过去几个世纪里“幸运的少数人”积累的知识。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: Education in the wilderness is not a matter of monetary means.
rows.zh: 荒野中的教育，不是钱财多寡的问题。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: All are entitled to an equal start.
rows.zh: 所有人都有权享有平等的起点。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: There is none of the hurry which, in our society, often hampers the full development of a growing personality.
rows.zh: 那里没有我们社会中的那种催赶，而这种催赶往往妨碍成长中的人格得到充分发展。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: There, a child grows up under the ever-present attention of his parents; therefore the jungles and the savannahs know of no ‘juvenile delinquency’.
rows.zh: 在那里，孩子在父母始终如一的关照下成长；所以，丛林和草原上没有“青少年犯罪”。
rows.speaker: 旁白

rows.en: No necessity of making a living away from home results in neglect of children, and no father is confronted with his inability to ‘buy’ an education for his child.
rows.zh: 父母不必因外出谋生而疏于照顾孩子，也没有哪个父亲会面对自己无力为孩子“买”教育的困境。
rows.speaker: 旁白

usage.note: 用于说明回报、帮助等具体采取的形式。
usage.example: Convinced of the importance of education, modern states ‘invest’ in institutions of learning to get back ‘interest’ in the form of a large group of enlightened young men and women who are potential leaders.
usage.exampleZh: 现代国家确信教育的重要性，于是向教育机构“投资”，以一大批思想开明、具有领导潜能的青年男女作为收回的“利息”。

usage.exampleZh: 我们会较少重视“事实和数字”，而更重视良好的记忆力、实用心理知识，以及人与其他公民和睦相处的能力。

usage.note: 后接人，通常指能和睦交往；也可加 well 表示相处融洽。

usage.note: 可直接接 that 从句，此处省略 that。
